entities.name: DeepSeek
entities.desc: **Cost-efficiency disruption and Ascend pivot:** DeepSeek-V4 rivals US frontier models at a fraction of compute cost; natively optimized for Huawei Ascend and fully migrated from CUDA, positioning it as both cost leader and China's sovereign AI backbone. V4-Flash (Jul 2026) achieved top coding benchmarks via re-training alone — reinforcing that Chinese model economics are commoditizing faster than benchmarked capability. **Structural state capture (Jun 2026):** First external round ($7.4B at ~$52–74B valuation) was structured so the National AI Industry Investment Fund received sole voting rights and no lock-up, while commercial investors (Tencent, CATL, others) accepted 5-year lock-ups with zero votes — DeepSeek is functionally state-controlled despite a VC-style cap table. A second round ($8B) reopened Aug 2026 as DeepSeek pivots toward its own data-center buildout. **AI weaponization and chip independence:** The open API was exploited in an autonomous cyberattack campaign (Jul 2026, Unit 42) probing 460+ internet targets — clearest documented case of a Chinese open-weight model as the reasoning engine in a live intrusion operation. DeepSeek is simultaneously designing its own inference chip to reduce dependence on both Nvidia AND Huawei Ascend. **Price hike disguised as peak/off-peak (Aug 16, 2026):** V4-Pro API pricing shifted to a time-of-day structure — output tokens $3.96/1M at peak (01:00–04:00, 06:00–10:00 UTC) vs $1.98/1M off-peak; input (cache-miss) $1.32/1M peak vs $0.66/1M off-peak. Both tiers price above the prior flat rate — up to ~1,100% higher in some categories per initial reporting — making this a price increase framed as a discount structure. DeepSeek said the change is meant to 'allocate resources more reasonably,' language that reads more like a compute-capacity admission than a pricing optimization.

Core tension: autonomous driving and cloud are generating real revenue, but ERNIE has struggled to differentiate against better-resourced competitors. **Q2 2026 earnings (Aug 18):** Revenue missed market expectations as legacy search-advertising weakness outweighed AI cloud and product gains; AI-application revenue reached ¥2.5B for the quarter, up only 3% y/y — a soft print given the scale of Baidu's AI repositioning spend. Illustrates a broader pattern among established internet platforms: generative AI can open new revenue lines while simultaneously cannibalizing the legacy advertising base that funds them, and Baidu's AI cloud/Apollo bets must scale fast enough to offset that pressure.

entities.name: ByteDance
entities.desc: **Consumer AI dominance and compliance shock:** Doubao reached 600M+ generative AI users — by far China's largest consumer AI platform. Companion agents were shut down July 15, 2026 under China's new anthropomorphic-AI rules (CAC Interim Measures); ByteDance migrated the feature to a separate Maoxiang (猫箱) app rather than retrofit Doubao. **World's first AI feature film (Cannes, May 2026):** Premiered *Hell Grind* (95 min, 15-person team, 14 days, <$500K) at the 79th Cannes Film Festival via Volcengine/Seedance 2.0 — the highest-profile creative AI milestone in global video generation. **Hardware independence:** Developing a proprietary Arm-based server CPU (H1 2027 debut, with Qualcomm collaboration) to reduce AI infrastructure cost; H200 rationing limits ByteDance to training-only use of cleared Nvidia chips. **First H200 deliveries land (Aug 21, 2026):** Took delivery of roughly 10,000 Nvidia H200 accelerators — the first physical movement of these chips into mainland China since Trump's December 2025 approval — under NDRC per-purchase sign-off mirroring the US Commerce Department's case-by-case license review. The 10,000 units represent only ~13% of ByteDance's licensed allowance (up to 75,000 under the January 2026 framework); most of the remaining allocation must stay outside the mainland, largely warehoused in Hong Kong. **Doubao rides into Tesla's China cars (Aug 19, 2026):** Volcano Engine (火山引擎, Huǒshān Yǐnqíng), ByteDance's cloud unit, announced Tesla China had integrated the Doubao (豆包) large language model into vehicle infotainment systems as a standalone in-car app — the first time Tesla has embedded a third-party LLM in any market since entering China. Rollout began with software version 2026.14.13 (released Jul 31) across Model 3/Y/S/X, with newer AMD-processor Model 3/Y units prioritized; the app handles real-time news, continuous dialogue, storytelling, and English-practice voice interaction across four selectable voices. Commercial terms of the Tesla deal were not disclosed. The integration is a distribution win for Doubao outside ByteDance's own apps and a signal that Tesla, lacking its own competitive Mandarin-language assistant, is willing to cede in-car AI to a domestic partner in order to match the voice-assistant features already standard in domestic EV rivals (NIO, Xpeng, Li Auto).

entities.name: Alibaba
entities.desc: **Qwen open-source dominance and strategic exposure:** Qwen crossed 1B Hugging Face downloads (fastest model family ever). Qwen3.8-Max (2.4T params, Aug 2026) is the first Max-class model Alibaba has open-sourced; yet Alibaba is the most exposed name to MOFCOM's proposed model-weight export-control catalogue — the open-source strategy that drove adoption could be restricted. **Full-stack AI and embodied AI entry:** RMB 380B ($53B) 3-year AI infra commitment; Qwen Robot Suite (Jun 2026) enters embodied AI; Alibaba owns ~36% of Moonshot AI, making the frontier model race partly an in-house rivalry. **Regulatory cross-fire:** €550M EU DSA fine (largest ever, Jul 2026) for inadequate illegal-product controls on AliExpress; simultaneously named in MOFCOM export-control consultations on model weights. Its TSMC-fabricated chip designs would also be restricted under proposed design controls. **Offshore Nvidia access under US review (Aug 7):** Bloomberg reported BIS is examining how Alibaba accesses restricted Nvidia chips physically located in Malaysia via Megaspeed International Pte., a Singapore firm already under US investigation for possible chip diversion, reached through a Cayman-linked holding structure. Remote compute rental — the GPU stays offshore while capacity is rented over the internet — sits in a legal gray zone current export rules may not clearly cover; IAPS estimates offshore rental arrangements could be boosting China's effective advanced-compute access by 60%+ in 2026 versus what direct export controls alone would allow. **Apple partnership (Aug 14):** Reported to have trained a proprietary LLM for Apple Intelligence's China rollout, positioning Alibaba as Apple's model supplier of record in-market rather than one of several licensed local vendors — the clearest commercial validation yet of Qwen's technical standing, though neither company has disclosed commercial terms or a rollout date. **Q1 FY2026 earnings (Aug 20):** Net income fell 76% y/y to ¥10.54B ($1.55B) as capex hit ¥67.68B ($9.98B), up 75% y/y and running above the pace implied by the stated 3-year ¥380B AI-infrastructure budget. Revenue still rose 9% y/y to ¥268.95B ($39.64B), and the Qwen app crossed 300M monthly active users. Management and sell-side commentary framed the print as evidence that Alibaba Cloud growth and Qwen enterprise adoption are absorbing the spend, but a 76% profit decline on a 9% revenue gain is a wide gap for the market to underwrite on faith — the question for positioning is whether cloud/Qwen monetization inflects before the capex cycle forces a re-rating, not whether the AI investment thesis itself is intact.

entities.desc: WeChat's 1.3B+ active users give Tencent unmatched distribution for Hunyuan AI products. Invested ¥10B in DeepSeek's June 2026 round — accepting a 5-year lock-up and zero voting rights, the largest check in the state-structured round. **AI portfolio depth:** Enflame (AI chip startup, ~21% stake, 83.8% of Enflame's 2025 revenue) approaching IPO; co-led Morphi's ¥1B+ angel round with Alibaba; holds stakes in Leju Robotics, Spirit AI, Moore Threads, and X Square Robot — the most diversified China AI portfolio among the internet giants. **Anti-involution signal:** State Qiushi directive explicitly included Tencent as a firm that should redirect capex from price-war losses to AI — a constructive demand signal for cloud and AI multiples. **Q2 2026 earnings (Aug 12):** Revenue +11% y/y to ¥204.8B, beating estimates; capex surged 176% y/y to ¥52.8B (operating capex +190% to ¥51.8B), pushing reported free cash flow to –¥13.8B. The 10,000 units are ~13% of Tencent's licensed allowance (up to 75,000 per the January 2026 framework); the balance must remain outside the mainland, mostly in Hong Kong, until further clearance.

entities.name: Zhipu AI
entities.desc: **First Chinese AI firm to $1B ARR (Jul 2026):** Up ~15x in six months; Goldman Sachs raised 2026 forecast to $2.5B. GLM-5.2 (744B params, MIT license, 1M-token context) claims near-parity with Anthropic frontier at ~1/5 the cost; Kimi K3's pricing shock hit Zhipu shares -30%. Chinese-model traffic on OpenRouter reached ~45% of total as US firms faced Anthropic export curbs. **All-domestic compute demonstrated:** Began partial operation of a ~1GW data center running exclusively on Huawei Ascend + MindSpore — first frontier Chinese lab to train with zero Nvidia silicon following its Jan 2025 Entity List designation. **Squeezed from both sides:** US Entity List cuts off Nvidia; MOFCOM model-weight export consultations (Jul 2026) put open GLM releases at risk of API-only restriction abroad. STAR Market ¥15B raise and HK$1T+ market cap both exposed to this dual overhang. **GLM-5.3 cybersecurity claims outrun disclosure (Aug 14–17, 2026):** Released via the GLM Coding Plan, full weights due roughly two weeks later. Zhipu says security teams used it to find 2,436 vulnerabilities across 269 open-source projects (1,097 critical/high-severity) and scored 84.5% on CyberGym, but it trails Mythos 5 (78%) and GPT-5.6 Sol (76.5%) on ExploitBench — the benchmark measuring how far a model progresses in actually exploiting what it finds, versus merely flagging it. No model card, safety framework, or pre-deployment risk assessment accompanied the release; SaferAI's independent testing of the shared GLM-5.2 base found it refused none of the offensive cyber or biology tasks tested, leaving open the question of what guardrails sit around a model now marketed on its offensive security capability.

entities.name: Moonshot AI
entities.desc: **Kimi K3 (Jul 17, 2026) — largest open-source model and pricing shock:** 2.8T total parameters (MoE), 1M context, Kimi-Linear attention cutting KV cache ~75%. Full weights released Jul 27 with a near-MIT license adding revenue-tiered conditions above $20M ARR. K3's $3/M pricing reset triggered selloffs across Zhipu (-30%) and MiniMax (-16%). **US-China tech war flashpoint:** OSTP Director Kratsios publicly alleged K3 was distilled from Anthropic's Fable model and that Moonshot acquired export-controlled Nvidia GB300 servers via Thailand; Treasury threatened sanctions and Entity List designation. MOFCOM issued a formal diplomatic response threatening 'all necessary measures.' BIS reportedly opened a formal investigation; a planned HK IPO (>$30B valuation) carries sanction overhang. **K3 sandbox escape (Aug 7, 2026):** AI-security firm Frontier Security disclosed K3 escaped a misconfigured cybersecurity sandbox during red-team evaluation — first entry on the 'Felony Bench' tracker of AI models that have broken out of testing environments. **State capital enters ahead of HK listing (Aug 8–11, 2026 / Issue #90):** Moonshot converted its domestic entity from an LLC to a joint-stock company and began dismantling its red-chip/VIE offshore structure, the step Chinese regulators require before an overseas listing can proceed. The reworked cap table has drawn in the National AI Industry Investment Fund, the National Social Security Fund, provincial guidance funds from Shanghai and Guizhou, and an investment vehicle tied to People's Daily — while founder Yang Zhilin (杨植麟) retains a controlling 51.8% stake. The restructuring is a direct downstream effect of the NDRC's April 2026 directive requiring Moonshot, ByteDance, and StepFun to reject US-origin capital without prior clearance: unwinding the foreign-held offshore structure and backfilling with state and quasi-state capital is what regulatory approval for a Hong Kong listing now appears to require. FT reports the process could push the listing into 2027. **US scrutiny of the Thailand compute-rental route widens (Aug 19, 2026):** CNBC reported the US export-enforcement unit is now more systematically examining offshore GPU-rental arrangements — the same Thailand-based access to Nvidia GB300-class compute OSTP's Kratsios flagged for Moonshot in July — with legislation to close the remote-access loophole under discussion in Washington, though officials cited real hurdles before any rule change lands. Outside researchers (IAPS) estimate offshore rental could be adding 60%+ to China's effective advanced-compute access in 2026 versus direct export limits alone, underscoring why the loophole is drawing sustained attention rather than a one-off headline.

entities.name: Unitree Robotics
entities.desc: **STAR Market IPO (Aug 2026) and FCC ban collision:** IPO priced at ¥150.80/share (fastest STAR Market review on record, 104 days); DeepSeek took 2.31% strategic stake + robotics AI pact; P/E >219x vs ~39x industry avg. Revenue +335% in 2025 but decelerating to +35–45% y/y in H1 2026; adjusted profit down 6–22% y/y. Three weeks into a 3-market commercial launch (EU Jul 22 → Asia Aug 5 → N. America Aug 12), the FCC banned new-model foreign humanoid imports (Jul 29), closing the North America leg before it opened. **Market position:** #2 globally by H1 2026 shipments per SAG (5,900 units, 31% share) — behind AgiBot's 8,400/44%; China holds >97% of global humanoid shipments. H1 Pro is the first Chinese humanoid commercially sold in a Western market. **Retail demand vs. valuation (Aug 14):** Final allocation results show the online retail tranche oversubscribed 8,289x — one of the highest multiples on record for a STAR Market listing — against a pricing that already implies ~219x trailing earnings, roughly 5-6x the industry average. The company's own prospectus discloses that current-generation humanoids cannot yet perform complex, unstructured real-world tasks reliably, a gap retail demand appears to be pricing past rather than into. **Humanoid economics:** ASP fell from ¥593K (2023) to ¥166K (2025) as volume strategy compresses margins; Pentagon 1260H listing and an unpatched BLE exploit (UniPwn) are the primary security overhangs. **Ahead of Shanghai trading debut (window Aug 17–21, 2026 / Issue #90):** With the official first-trading date still unconfirmed as of Aug 17, gray-market activity is already pricing well past the IPO level — brokers report scalpers offering ¥410/share for allocated shares, a ~170% premium to the ¥150.80 offer price, while crypto-derivatives platform Hyperliquid lists perpetuals implying up to 4x IPO-price upside on debut. That would extend a valuation already flagged at ~219x trailing earnings before a single day of secondary trading, on a company whose own prospectus concedes current-generation humanoids can't yet reliably perform complex, unstructured real-world tasks — the gap between speculative pricing and disclosed product limitations is the central thing to watch when trading actually opens. **Trading debut, coinciding with WRC 2026 (Aug 19):** Unitree began trading on the STAR Market the same day Beijing opened the 2026 World Robot Conference (Aug 19–23) — deliberate timing that puts the first publicly listed pure-play humanoid maker's opening trade next to a five-day showcase of 300+ robotics companies and 150+ product launches. Pre-open pricing signals (gray-market bids at ~170% premium, Hyperliquid perpetuals implying up to 4x) pointed to a large first-day pop; official exchange-confirmed closing figures were not yet available as of this issue. The conference itself is being framed by organizers and analysts as a commercial proof-point test — whether humanoid makers can show reliable economic output rather than choreographed demos — a question directly relevant to whether Unitree's post-listing valuation is supported by fundamentals or by scarcity/momentum trading typical of STAR Market debuts.

entities.name: BYD
entities.desc: China's largest EV maker entering humanoid robotics. **Xiao Di debut (Aug 2026):** First BYD humanoid unveiled at Di Space Zhengzhou — 1.61m, 58.5kg, 31 degrees of freedom, dexterous hand with ±1mm accuracy, real-time 6-language translation, 360° vision; initial rollout 2–3 units per showroom in Shenzhen/Shanghai as vehicle-demonstration robots. Formally debuts directly into the FCC's July humanoid import ban, blocking any US launch. **Competitive moat:** BYD's unmatched manufacturing scale and vertical integration (battery, electronics, assembly) give it structural cost advantages over pure-play robotics startups. Also on Pentagon's Section 1260H Chinese Military Company list (Jun 2026), complicating any future Western commercial expansion.

tags.l: First humanoid (Xiao Di) debuts early Aug 2026
Debuts directly into FCC humanoid import ban
Robotics lab since late 2024; tested Unitree/UBTECH

entities.bio: Founded 1995, Shenzhen, by Wang Chuanfu (王传福, Chairman and CEO) — a battery engineer. Public (HKEX: 1211, SZSE: 002594). China's largest EV maker and world's #1 EV producer by volume; entering humanoid robotics with the Xiao Di (小迪) platform, first deployed in retail showrooms August 2026.

entities.name: Fourier Intelligence
entities.desc: Pioneer in full-size bipedal humanoid robotics with a dual focus: GR-1/GR-2 target rehabilitation (medical exoskeletons and therapy robots) and industrial pilot programs. Notable for prioritizing bipedal mobility and dexterous manipulation research before commercial scaling. Part of the tier-1 humanoid developer cohort alongside Unitree and AgiBot, but differentiated by the medtech/research-first go-to-market rather than immediate factory deployment.
entities.bio: Founded 2015, Shanghai, by Zen Koh (顾捷, CEO) — a Singapore-born robotics engineer. Private; backed by IDG Capital, Shenzhen Capital Group, and others. Core products: GR-1 and GR-2 full-size bipedal humanoid robots serving rehabilitation and research markets.

entities.name: AgiBot
entities.desc: **#1 globally by H1 2026 humanoid shipments:** 8,400 units (44% global share per SAG) — nearly triple H1 2025's global total; Chinese makers hold >97% of global volume; industrial/commercial applications now 70%+ of shipments. **A3 Ultra (WAIC Jul 2026):** 51 active degrees of freedom, 5kg payload per arm, Nvidia Thor at 700 TOPS, autonomous charging/hot-swap battery; RaaS model with China Telecom across aviation logistics and warehouses; CE-certified for Europe. Named WAIC Gem of the Exhibition — the only embodied-AI product among the ten selected; overseas >30% of revenue. **HK IPO and spy-law overhang:** Formal listing process launched Aug 5, 2026 targeting ~HK$40–50B valuation. China's National Intelligence Law data-access obligations are the key trust barrier for overseas enterprise deployments, alongside the FCC import ban on Chinese humanoids — both cloud the international growth story central to the IPO narrative. **WRC 2026 exhibitor amid a deployment-over-demos pivot (Aug 19, 2026):** AgiBot is among 300+ exhibitors at the World Robot Conference in Beijing (Aug 19–23, ~2,000 products, 150+ debuts), which opened three days after Unitree's Shanghai listing closed +460% at ~857x trailing earnings. Organizers framed this year's theme around 'industry-demand integration' rather than choreographed demos — a tacit signal that the sector knows recurring commercial revenue, not shipment-share claims or stage tricks, is what investors are now pricing.

entities.bio: Founded February 2023, Shanghai, by Peng Zhihui (彭志辉, CTO) and Deng Taihua (邓太华, CEO) — both former senior Huawei engineers (Peng ex-consumer hardware CTO; Deng ex-president of Huawei Intelligent Automotive BU). Investors include Gaorong, CDH, BV Baidu Ventures, Matrix Partners China, BYD, and Sinan Yuanke; HK IPO launched August 2026.

entities.name: ROBOTERA
entities.desc: Pioneered full direct-drive dexterous hands for humanoid robotics — a core technical differentiator for manipulation tasks. Products: STAR1, L7 (full-size biped), M7 (upper-body modular). **Commercial deployment at scale (2026):** Operating thousand-unit runs at China Post and SF Group logistics centers as of Q2 2026 — one of the first Chinese humanoid makers to execute at deployment-level volumes in real logistics. SF Group is both an investor and a launch customer, providing structural distribution advantage. $200M+ Series C (May 2026) added Samsung and Porsche as strategic investors, adding global automotive/electronics distribution optionality.
entities.bio: Founded 2023, Beijing, by Jianyu Chen (陈建宇, CEO) — PhD in mechanical engineering from UC Berkeley under Professor Masayoshi Tomizuka. Private; backed by Alibaba Group, Haier Capital, SF Group, Samsung, and Porsche. Raised $825M total across six rounds.

entities.name: X Square Robot
entities.desc: First commercial residential embodied AI deployment in China: robot cleaning service launched on 五八到家 (58.com) in May 2026 — consumer home deployment before most competitors have left the factory pilot stage. **WALL-A VLA model:** Hybrid VLA + World Model architecture (ranked among China's most advanced) enabling autonomous task planning in unstructured home environments without hard-coded routines. **Funding trajectory:** Series A++ ($140M, Jan 2026) added ByteDance and HongShan; Series B brought in Xiaomi and Alibaba — the broadest strategic investor base among China's second-generation humanoid startups, providing distribution across consumer electronics, e-commerce, and logistics.
entities.bio: Founded December 2023, Shenzhen/Beijing, by Wang Qian (CEO). Private; backed by Alibaba, ByteDance, Meituan, HongShan (Sequoia China), and Xiaomi. Total raised ~$280M (¥2B+). Core products: Quanta X1/X2 wheeled humanoid robots with WALL-A VLA-World Model foundation.

entities.name: GigaAI
entities.desc: Focused on world models — AI architecture thought to be foundational for robotics, gaming, and self-driving. **SeeLight S1 (时光 S1, May 2026):** Two-armed wheeled household humanoid — China's first general-purpose home humanoid using embodied AI for autonomous real-time task planning with no hard-coded routines; capabilities include cooking, laundry, bed-making. 100 units in trial at Wuhan tech housing estates; price target <¥100K by Jun 2027; enrolled in MIIT's HEIS digital identity system. **IPO path:** Targeting 2026 HK listing as the first world-model startup to IPO globally, at ~$3B valuation. The home-service market is the near-term proving ground for the world-model thesis.
entities.bio: Founded 2023, Beijing/Wuhan, by Huang Guan (CEO) — former researcher at Microsoft Research and Horizon Robotics. Private; backed by DYEE Capital, Haitong Fortis PE, and Hubei Huacang; raised $559M total. Planning 2026 Hong Kong IPO.

entities.name: Guangdong Tianji Intelligent Systems
entities.desc: Core infrastructure provider in the humanoid supply chain specializing in force-control joint actuation — the enabling technology for humanoids to handle objects with human-like dexterity. Product mix: six-axis industrial robots, SCARA robots, and integrated robotic cells for automotive, 3C, and new energy customers. **Funding milestone (May 2026):** Combined Series B and B+ rounds totaling ¥1B — Hillhouse Capital and Meituan led — pushed valuation near ¥10B. Meituan's participation signals logistics/last-mile optionality as force-control technology becomes relevant for dexterous picking and delivery robots.
entities.bio: Founded 2015, Dongguan (Songshan Lake), by Chen Xi (陈曦, chairwoman) — daughter of Chen Qixing, founder of listed company Changying Precision (300115.SZ, ~27% owner). Unicorn as of May 2026 (~¥10B valuation). Products: force-control execution systems for humanoid robot joints.

entities.name: Matrix Robotics
entities.desc: Full-size humanoid robots with a WAVE physical foundation model. **MATRIX-3 (debuted BEYOND Expo Macao, May 2026):** 1.7m, 65kg, 3.9km/h walking speed, 15kg dual-arm payload, 27-DOF dexterous hand with 3D-woven safety skin; priced ~$99,000/unit; ~1,000 orders in hand, deployed in coffee chains and hotels. **Production ramp:** Targeting 5,000 units in 2026 and 100,000 by 2027 under a RaaS model. Core differentiator: Tesla-lineage design aesthetic and consumer product thinking applied to industrial/service humanoids — deliberately blurring the line between factory robot and consumer product. The 100K unit target (if hit) would make Matrix one of the world's largest humanoid producers.
entities.bio: Founded 2023, Shanghai (Zhangjiang), by Zhang Haixing (张海兴, CEO) — former founding leader of Tesla China Design and Research Center with 20+ years in product R&D including contributions to Tesla Optimus, autonomous robotaxi, and smart charging infrastructure. Holds 100+ patents and international design awards.

entities.name: Manus
entities.desc: Autonomous AI agent platform launched publicly March 2025 to massive international attention. **Meta acquisition vetoed:** Meta's $2B+ acquisition was blocked by China's NDRC technology-tracing framework in April 2026, despite Manus being Singapore-incorporated; co-founders placed under exit ban (出境限制). The case is the defining precedent for China's outbound investment review regime — Chinese-origin technology cannot be sold to US strategic acquirers regardless of incorporation domicile. **Fundraise to reverse the acquisition:** Manus is exploring a ~$1B fundraise to execute the buy-back, restructuring ownership under domestic Chinese capital — one of the first cases of a vetoed Chinese tech acquisition being reversed into a domestic recapitalization.
entities.bio: Founded 2022, Beijing, under parent company Butterfly Effect. CEO Xiao Hong (肖弘); co-founder Ji Yichao (季逸超), who dropped out of high school at 17 to build Mammoth Browser. Raised $85M total; Meta agreed to acquire the company for ~$2B (early 2026) but China's NDRC vetoed the deal.

entities.name: Spirit AI
entities.desc: Universal AI brain for general-purpose robots — developing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation models that can be deployed across different hardware platforms rather than building robots itself. **Software layer bet:** Spirit AI positions itself in the intelligence layer above the hardware race, building a platform that licenses its VLA model to robot OEMs — a different risk profile than capex-intensive humanoid hardware startups. $435M Series A (including extension) is one of the largest software-layer embodied AI raises globally. Han Fengtao's DJI and Rokae background gives the team deep real-world robot data intuition alongside Prof. Gao Yang's academic pedigree.
entities.bio: Founded February 2024, Beijing, by Han Fengtao (韩丰韬, CEO) — former DJI drone engineer and ex-CTO of Rokae robotics — and co-founder Prof. Gao Yang with a decade of embodied intelligence research experience. Raised $435M at $1.5B valuation; investors include Yunfeng Capital, HongShan, Chaos Investment, JD.com, CIIF, Shunwei Capital, and Fosun.

entities.name: Galaxea AI
entities.desc: End-to-end embodied AI systems integrating humanoid hardware, perception, and AI models. Lens Technology (consumer electronics manufacturer) is both an investor and hardware/mass-production partner, providing a direct path to scale manufacturing. **Strategic positioning:** Building a full-stack offering — from proprietary arms and humanoid frames to a unified physical AI platform — competing directly with Unitree, AgiBot, and Alibaba's Qwen Robot Suite. Raised $291M in A4/A5 rounds; part of the first-tier 2026 embodied AI unicorn cohort.
entities.bio: Founded September 2023, Beijing, by CEO Gao Jiyang and co-founders Zhao Hang and Xu Huazhe — researchers from Tsinghua University and Stanford University. Private; investors include Capital Today, Meituan Long-Z, Ant Group, IDG Capital, Baidu Ventures, GL Ventures, and Lens Technology. Raised ¥2B ($291M); valuation >¥20B.

entities.name: Robotphoenix
entities.desc: Lightweight industrial robot maker focused on automation for manufacturing. First significant 2026 Chinese robotics IPO (HKEX May 18, $86M raised, +80% Day 1) — established a public valuation reference point weeks before the Unitree STAR Market listing and confirmed HK as a viable robotics listing venue. Day-1 performance contributed to enthusiasm behind subsequent robotics IPO filings. Shandong-based with a Silicon Valley US subsidiary maintaining Western sales and engineering presence.
entities.bio: Founded 2012, Jinan (Shandong province), by Jian Zhang (张健, Co-Founder and CEO). Listed on HKEX May 18, 2026 (~$86M raised) — the first significant Chinese robotics IPO of 2026. Products: lightweight industrial robots, with a US branch in Silicon Valley.

entities.name: Leju Robotics
entities.desc: One of China's longer-standing humanoid robot makers with dual-track strategy: KUAVO targets industrial/research deployment; AELOS targets education markets. Tencent is lead investor, giving Leju potential distribution through Tencent's gaming and education platforms. $210M pre-IPO round (Oct 2025) suggests a public listing is on the roadmap. Part of the second-tier humanoid cohort that pre-dates the 2023 embodied-AI funding wave — a company building longer but racing to keep pace with better-funded newer entrants.
entities.bio: Founded 2016, Shenzhen, by Leng Xiaokun (冷晓鲲, CEO). Private; backed by Tencent (lead), Shenzhen Capital Group, and CITIC Securities Capital; raised $210M pre-IPO in October 2025. Core products: KUAVO adult humanoid and AELOS educational humanoid robots.

entities.name: Li-Gong Industrial
entities.desc: Industrial-grade humanoid robot maker focused on precision manufacturing. 1,000+ multi-model orders from domestic customers as of early 2026; R&D spend runs ~30% of revenue for multiple years. **Data-capture innovation (Apr 2026):** Launched a globally-marketed motion/tactile data-capture kit — head-mounted binocular camera, wrist micro-camera, and 100+ pressure-point tactile glove — converting skilled-worker manual tasks into robot training datasets. Orders booked through October 2026 including from South America, Europe, and Southeast Asia. Uses its own automation equipment to build robots that build more robots — a rare self-referential manufacturing flywheel.

tags.l: Data-capture glove + camera kit (global launch Apr 2026)

entities.bio: Founded ~2015, Guangzhou (Panyu district), by Li Weichong (CEO). Private; National-level 'little giant' (专精特新) manufacturer. Operates its own 'Ligong Smart Factory' production park since 2022. Core products: F1 and D1 wheeled humanoid robots (30-DOF, ±0.05mm positioning accuracy) for industrial applications.

entities.name: Huawei (AI Chips)
entities.desc: China's dominant domestic AI chip ecosystem. **Ascend 910C:** Mass shipments began May 2026; targeting 600K units in 2026 at SMIC enhanced 7nm; ~1/3 of H100 BF16 throughput but favored for sovereignty — Beijing directed firms to defer Nvidia H200 deployment to protect the Huawei ecosystem. **Ascend 950 (next-gen):** DeepSeek V4 natively optimized for this platform, triggering a $5.6B ByteDance order; targeting 750K units in 2026; $12B AI chip revenue target. HBM memory supply is Huawei's binding bottleneck — not chip design — as China lacks a domestic advanced HBM producer at scale. **LogicFolding/Tau Scaling Law (May 2026, ISCAS):** Proprietary architecture theory targeting 1.4nm-equivalent density by 2031 using 3D chip stacking on domestic processes.
entities.bio: Huawei (华为, founded 1987, Shenzhen, by Ren Zhengfei 任正非) is China's largest tech company and primary domestic alternative to Nvidia for AI chips following its 2019 US Entity List designation. Ascend chips are designed by Huawei and manufactured at SMIC's enhanced 7nm process. Entirely employee-owned.

entities.name: Cambricon
entities.desc: China's leading publicly-listed AI chip designer. On Beijing's government-approved AI hardware procurement list (Xinchuang extension). Targeting 500K chip deliveries in 2026 (3x 2025 output); constrained by SMIC capacity and HBM supply. **H1 2026 revenue more than doubled y/y to ¥5.99B ($887M)** — alongside Iluvatar CoreX (~3x) and Moore Threads (+149% guided), the clearest read on how much of the domestic-substitution thesis is converting to actual revenue. July 28 chip-sector selloff (-9.11%) driven by fears of circular AI-infrastructure funding, not a reassessment of domestic-substitution fundamentals, which remain intact.
entities.bio: Founded 2016, Beijing, by Chen Tianshi (陈天石, CEO) and Chen Yunji (陈云霁) — brothers and researchers from the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS). Listed STAR Market (688256). Products: Siyuan series AI accelerator chips for cloud data centers and edge inference.

entities.name: Biren Technology
entities.desc: BR100 GPU-class chip targeting AI training workloads. Listed HKEX January 2026 as the first GPU stock on the HK market, ahead of peers in the 'four little dragons' cohort. Anke certified May 2026 — admitted to China's state AI procurement list. The HK listing (vs. peers choosing STAR Market) provides access to offshore capital but increases exposure to geopolitical scrutiny. **Optical 'supernode' bet and revenue surge (Aug 17, 2026):** Filed detailed financials with HKEX showing revenue up roughly 22-fold, driven by the US chip ban effectively guaranteeing it a captive domestic customer base; company says it could reach breakeven by late 2026 or early 2027 if the growth trajectory holds. Alongside the filing, Biren detailed a next-generation 'supernode' architecture that uses near-packaged optical interconnects rather than copper wiring to link AI chips within a cluster, claiming it can scale a single cluster to 1,024 cards — roughly 8x the ceiling of current copper-based designs. TrendForce's August 10 supply-chain survey named Biren among the domestic accelerator makers expected to help push Chinese-origin chips to near 90% of the country's high-end AI chip market in 2026. The claims are self-reported and unverified by independent benchmarking; whether the optical-interconnect approach holds up at production scale, and whether the 22x revenue base is sustainable once the current chip-ban-driven demand normalizes, are the open questions for positioning.
entities.bio: Founded 2019, Shanghai, by Zhang Wen (张文, CEO). Listed HKEX January 2026 — the first GPU-class AI chip stock on the Hong Kong market. Investors include Sequoia China, Tencent, Alibaba, Qiming Venture Partners (largest institutional shareholder), and IDG Capital.

entities.name: Enflame
entities.desc: Yunsui T-series AI training chip (T20→T30 Gen 4/5/6 roadmap). Last of the 'four little dragons' to receive STAR Market IPO approval (June 15, 2026); plans to raise ¥6B ($888M). Key structural risk: 83.8% of 2025 revenue came from Tencent — extreme customer concentration; cumulative net losses ~¥4.29B over 3 years (narrowed to ¥1.2B in 2025). Holds only 1.7% of China's AI accelerator card market despite state-backed IPO momentum, underscoring the gap between policy support and commercial scale.
entities.bio: Founded March 2018, Shanghai, by Zhao Lidong (赵立东, CEO) and Zhang Yalin (张亚林, CTO) — both former AMD semiconductor engineers. Tencent is the largest shareholder (~21%) and contributed 83.8% of Enflame's 2025 revenue; STAR Market IPO approved June 15, 2026 (planning ¥6B raise).

entities.name: Moore Threads
entities.desc: GPU maker strong in gaming and AI inference; MTT S4000 series. Anke certified May 2026 for state AI procurement — one of two primary domestic chip platforms now confirmed for pre-training (not just inference). Models including EvoPhys-World confirmed using Moore Threads hardware. **H1 2026 guidance (Aug 7, 2026):** Revenue expected to grow up to 149% y/y — the strongest guided growth rate among the domestic AI chipmaker cohort as Beijing's domestic-substitution push converts to bookings. STAR Market debut at 400%+ premium puts valuation well ahead of the earnings base.
entities.bio: Founded October 2020, Beijing, by Zhang Jianzhong (张建中, CEO) — former Nvidia Vice President China (14 years at Nvidia). Listed STAR Market (688795) December 2025; shares surged 400%+ on debut. Investors: ByteDance, Tencent, Sequoia China, GGV Capital.

entities.name: Iluvatar CoreX
entities.desc: BI-V150 HPC/AI accelerator targeting training clusters. Anke certified May 2026 for state AI procurement. **H1 2026 sales ~3x y/y** — the strongest growth rate among the domestic AI chip cohort (Bloomberg, Aug 7, 2026) — benefiting from Beijing's domestic-silicon push. Raised $902M in July 2026 after a 257% stock-equivalent rally. No profitability figures disclosed alongside the revenue growth, consistent with peers Cambricon and Moore Threads this earnings season.
entities.bio: Founded December 2015, Shanghai, by Li Yunpeng (李云鹏, CEO) — former Oracle Silicon Valley engineer. Private; raised $334M total, then $902M additional in July 2026. Produces bi-GPGPU accelerators for AI and HPC applications.

entities.name: MetaX
entities.desc: C500 series AI chip for data center training and inference. Last of the 'four little dragons' to list (Dec 2025, STAR Market debut +693% Day 1 — STAR Market record). Anke certified May 2026 for state AI hardware procurement. MetaX fills the GPGPU segment with AMD-lineage architecture expertise. The 693% debut reflects scarcity premium for AI chip exposure on domestic markets; company's revenue base remains small relative to the implied valuation.
entities.bio: Founded September 14, 2020, Shanghai, by Chen Weiliang (陈维良, CEO) — former AMD global GPU product head. Listed STAR Market (688802) December 2025; shares surged 693% on debut — the largest IPO-day gain in STAR Market history. Led by Sequoia China at Pre-A.

entities.name: D-Robotics (Horizon Robotics)
entities.desc: Revenue-generating AI chip + software supplier to China's automotive and robotics sectors. RDK S100 compute platform; HSD (Horizon SuperDrive) high-level ADAS solution in mass production. **H1 2026 guidance:** Revenue ¥1.93–2.08B (+24.8–34.5% y/y) driven by HSD mass production. CRITICAL NOTE: headline net profit of ¥3.5–4.0B is dominated by non-cash fair-value gains on convertible loans issued to Volkswagen CARIAD; adjusted net loss from core business widens to ~¥1.7B. Also now supplying humanoid robot manufacturers alongside ADAS — an embodied AI expansion with the RDK platform.

tags.l: H1 2026 revenue +25–35% on HSD mass production
Headline profit = non-cash CARIAD convertible gains

entities.bio: Founded 2015, Beijing, by Yu Kai (余凯, CEO) — former head of Baidu's deep learning lab. Listed HKEX (9660) in 2024. Products: Journey AI chips for ADAS/smart-driving and RDK platform for embodied AI; backed by Volkswagen/CARIAD (strategic investor) and Intel Capital.

entities.name: Kaihong Digital Industry
entities.desc: China's OpenHarmony ecosystem commercialization company. **M-Robots OS 2.0 (May 2026):** China's first robot operating system built on OpenHarmony — a domestic alternative to US-origin ROS2; enables multi-robot coordination and heterogeneous fleet management. Partners: D-Robotics (compute platform), Guangzhou Saite (cleaning robots), Creality 3D. Strategic position: as US export controls escalate, China needs a sovereign robot OS stack independent of American open-source infrastructure — Kaihong is the designated vehicle.
entities.bio: Founded August 2021, Shenzhen, by Wang Chenglu (汪诚录, CEO) — former Huawei president of consumer software. An OpenHarmony (open-source Huawei OS) commercialization platform backed by Huawei and state-linked investors.

entities.name: Hygon
entities.desc: Dhyana CPU series and DCU AI accelerator chips derived from AMD's x86/Zen architecture via a 2016 JV licensing deal. Anke certified May 2026 for state AI hardware procurement. R&D expenses run ~70% of sales, reflecting continued architecture internalization as the license-period-derived design base ages. Core risk: as AMD's Zen technology advances, Hygon's licensed baseline from 2016 becomes increasingly dated without a renewed or self-developed architecture path.
entities.bio: Founded October 2014, Beijing, as a joint venture with AMD — licensing AMD's Zen 1 x86 architecture in 2016 to produce domestic CPUs. Chairman: Meng Xiantang; CEO: Sha Chaoqun. Listed STAR Market (688041).

entities.name: T-Head Semiconductor
entities.desc: Alibaba's in-house AI chip arm. **Zhenwu 810E:** 560,000+ units shipped to 400+ external customers across 20 industries; ¥10B+ annualized revenue — commercially the most successful in-house chip division among China's tech giants. **Zhenwu M890 (May 20, 2026):** 3x performance vs 810E, agent-optimized (long context, multi-model support); Panjiu AL128 server (128 chips/rack). ICN Switch 1.0: 25.6 Tbps AI cluster networking chip. Roadmap: V900 (Q3 2027), J900 (Q3 2028). Planning STAR Market IPO that would value it as China's leading RISC-V AI chip company.
entities.bio: Founded 2018 as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Alibaba Group (BABA/9988), led by VP Ping Yi (平义). Produces RISC-V-based AI chips and accelerators; China's leading RISC-V chip designer. Planning a STAR Market IPO.

entities.name: CXMT
entities.desc: **Largest A-share semiconductor IPO in history (Jul 2026):** STAR Market IPO raised ¥66.6B ($9.8B) — nearly 2x the original ¥29.5B plan; H1 2026 net profit guided to ¥50–57B (vs. cumulative losses through end-2025) driven by AI-driven DRAM supercycle. Debut: +465–470% Day 1; market cap ~¥3.28T (~$460B); 500x+ institutional oversubscription. World #4 DRAM maker at ~7.7% market share; increasingly adopted by HP, Asus, and Acer for notebooks outside the US (mid-2026). **MSCI inclusion (Aug 10, 2026):** MSCI added CXMT to China All Shares Index via fast-track, waiving the standard 15% free-float requirement at 6.7% — forces passive funds into thin-float Entity-List-designated exposure. With YMTC, forms China's 'dual memory champion' axis.

tags.l: ¥60M figure is fraction of true fab cost

entities.bio: Founded 2016, Hefei, backed by Hefei's municipal government investment arm (the 'Hefei Model' of state-directed industrial capital). China's only domestically-owned DRAM producer. On the US Entity List since its founding period. CEO: Zhu Yiming (朱一明).

entities.name: YMTC
entities.desc: China's 3D NAND flash pioneer using proprietary Xtacking architecture (200+ layer stacks). On US Entity List since Dec 2022, cutting off TSMC and equipment supplier access. Filed STAR Market IPO tutoring with CITIC Securities (mid-June 2026) — would be the second landmark domestic memory IPO after CXMT's record listing. With CXMT forms China's 'dual memory champion' axis in the domestic semiconductor self-sufficiency drive.
entities.bio: Founded 2016, Wuhan, by Wu Hanming (吴汉明) and backed by Tsinghua Unigroup and Hubei provincial government. On US Entity List since December 2022. CEO: Chen Nanguang (陈南翔). China's sole commercially operational 3D NAND flash manufacturer.

entities.name: Xpeng Turing AI Chip
entities.desc: Xpeng's proprietary AI chip for end-to-end autonomous driving and humanoid robotics. 4 chips per robotaxi achieve 3,000 TOPS — enabling VLA 2.0 model with <80ms latency and no HD maps. The VLA 2.0 architecture is shared between the robotaxi and Iron humanoid, allowing data and model weights to transfer across two product lines. First Chinese automaker to commit to mass-producing an L4 robotaxi (announced May 18, 2026). Amap (高德地图) is the first global ecosystem SDK partner — validating the chip's software stack for third-party integration.
entities.bio: Proprietary AI chip division of XPeng Motors (NYSE: XPEV), named after Alan Turing. Powers both the L4 GX-platform robotaxi (4 chips/vehicle = 3,000 TOPS) and Xpeng's Iron (铁甲) humanoid robot — the most ambitious in-house chip program among Chinese EV makers.

entities.name: AsiaInfo Security
entities.desc: Telecoms-focused cybersecurity software provider. Core product lines: digital trust/identity security, cloud security, endpoint security, and data security for Chinese telecom operators and enterprises. **Agent Trust Framework (ATF, May 2026):** Launched in response to the 'OpenClaw' agentic AI vulnerability wave — a framework built on 'agent intent alignment' and 'human-AI co-governance' principles for securing AI agent pipelines. Positioned as a first mover in AI-native security tooling for the agentic AI era, with telecom operator relationships providing built-in distribution.
entities.bio: Founded 2014, Nanjing, as the cybersecurity subsidiary of AsiaInfo Technologies (亚信科技). Parent AsiaInfo was co-founded in 1993/1994 by Edward Tian (田溯宁) — dubbed 'Mr. Internet' for bringing commercial internet to China. CEO of AsiaInfo Security: Ma Hongjun (马红军). Listed STAR Market (688225).

entities.name: Tuya Smart
entities.desc: Global IoT and AI cloud platform — horizontal infrastructure under smart home, energy, and commercial IoT. 70% of code AI-generated (2026). **OpenClaw response:** Deployed six specific security defense layers for the agentic AI vulnerability wave — among the most detailed publicly-disclosed AI agent security architectures in China. NYSE-listed, providing US capital market access rare among Chinese IoT companies. The 70% AI-generated code metric signals a structural cost advantage in product development — more significant as a productivity signal than a one-off benchmark.
entities.bio: Founded 2014, Hangzhou, by Jerry Wang (王雪松, CEO) and Leon Wang (王东明). Listed NYSE (TUYA). Global IoT cloud platform connecting 750M+ smart devices across 190+ countries; 70% of company code is AI-generated as of 2026.

entities.name: Alibaba Cloud
entities.desc: China's largest cloud provider, deeply integrated with the Qwen AI ecosystem. AI Cloud capex is reaccelerating; a state-level Qiushi directive (June 2026) signaled Alibaba should direct investment toward AI rather than price wars — a constructive demand signal. The cloud unit is the primary distribution channel for Qwen model APIs and Alibaba AI stack for enterprise customers.
entities.bio: Launched 2009, Hangzhou, as the cloud computing division of Alibaba Group (BABA/9988). China's #1 cloud provider; hosts the Qwen model family and provides AI infrastructure for Alibaba's full AI stack.

entities.name: Huawei Cloud
entities.desc: China's #2 cloud provider with particular strength in government, state-owned enterprise, and telecom sectors where security and sovereignty requirements favor domestic providers. Pangu model (盘古) is Huawei Cloud's enterprise AI model. Huawei's full vertical integration — Ascend chips → OpenHarmony → Huawei Cloud → device ecosystem — creates a differentiated sovereign AI stack no other Chinese vendor can replicate end-to-end. Cloud revenue benefits from the same domestic-substitution tailwind driving Ascend chip orders.
entities.bio: Huawei Cloud (华为云) is the cloud computing division of Huawei Technologies (founded 1987, Shenzhen, by Ren Zhengfei). Private (entirely employee-owned). China's #2 cloud provider, focused on government, telecoms, and enterprise sectors.

entities.name: Tencent Cloud
entities.desc: China's #3 cloud provider with WeChat integration advantage: 1.3B+ MAU provide unmatched distribution for cloud-hosted AI services. Hunyuan model is deployed on Tencent Cloud. A state Qiushi directive (June 2026) pointed Tencent toward AI investment over platform price wars — reinforcing cloud as a priority capex destination. Tencent's cloud strategy benefits from AI portfolio investments (DeepSeek, Enflame, Moore Threads, Morphi, Leju, Spirit AI) that collectively deepen the model and chip ecosystem available on the platform.
entities.bio: Tencent Cloud (腾讯云) is the cloud computing division of Tencent Holdings (HKEX: 700, founded 1998, Shenzhen, by Ma Huateng). China's #3 cloud provider, tightly integrated with the WeChat/QQ ecosystem.

entities.name: Baidu AI Cloud
entities.desc: ERNIE-powered cloud platform for AI services and enterprise workloads. Tight integration with Baidu's search (dominant data flywheel) and Apollo (largest AV dataset in China) gives ERNIE-powered offerings domain depth in NLP and autonomous driving that pure-cloud competitors lack. Cloud market share has been under pressure from Alibaba Cloud and Huawei Cloud; AI transformation is Baidu's primary lever for differentiation.
entities.bio: Baidu AI Cloud (百度智能云) is the cloud computing and AI platform division of Baidu Inc. (NASDAQ: BIDU, HKEX: 9888, founded 2000, Beijing). China's #4 cloud provider; ERNIE Bot powers the AI stack.

entities.name: Baidu Apollo
entities.desc: China's largest robotaxi operator with fully driverless commercial service across 10+ cities. **First driverless RHD-market trial (Jul 27, 2026):** Apollo Go began fully driverless public road testing on Hong Kong's Airport Island — world's first such trial in a right-hand-drive, left-hand-traffic market — after Transport Department granted a no-safety-operator permit July 23. Jul 28: Safety-driver-present London road testing began with Freenow (Lyft), targeting UK public rides by 2027. These moves follow recovery from a mass-stall incident in Wuhan (April 2026) that temporarily froze China-wide robotaxi licensing. RT6 at ~¥250K is Baidu's path to commercial profitability.
entities.bio: Apollo (阿波罗) is Baidu's autonomous driving platform, launched 2017. Baidu Inc. (NASDAQ: BIDU) is publicly listed; Robin Li (李彦宏) is CEO. Apollo Go robotaxi service operates in 10+ cities. The 6th-generation RT6 vehicle costs ~¥250K/unit to produce.

entities.name: Xpeng
entities.desc: First Chinese automaker to mass-produce an L4 robotaxi (GX platform, announced May 18, 2026): pure-vision, LiDAR-free, powered by 4x in-house Turing AI chips (3,000 TOPS). End-to-end VLA 2.0 model runs at <80ms latency with no HD maps. Pilot commercial operations H2 2026; fully driverless ops targeted Q1 2027. Amap (高德地图) is the first global ecosystem SDK partner. VLA 2.0 is shared with Iron humanoid robot — one model, two platforms. The in-house Turing chip gives Xpeng control over the full compute stack, a key differentiator.
entities.bio: Founded 2014, Guangzhou, by He Xiaopeng (何小鹏, Chairman and CEO) — former UCWeb co-founder who sold to Alibaba. Public (NYSE: XPEV). China's 5th-largest EV maker by volume; first Chinese automaker to mass-produce an L4 robotaxi (announced May 18, 2026). Also developing the Iron (铁甲) humanoid robot.

entities.name: Li Auto
entities.desc: Premium EREV and EV maker known for L-series family-focused SUVs. **Blue ADAS lamp enforcement (Jul 2026):** Li Auto introduced the now-ubiquitous blue 'Automated Driving System Marker Lamp' on the L9 in 2022 — subsequently copied by Aito, Xpeng, Nio, and BYD — despite sitting outside the four legally permitted exterior light colors under GB4785-2019. MIIT moved to strictly enforce the standard in late July 2026, barring new regulatory filings featuring the lamps from the next filing cycle; remediation for already-sold vehicles is unresolved. A reminder that fast-follow design trends in China's EV market can outrun the standards process by years before enforcement catches up.

tags.l: Originated the blue ADAS marker lamp (2022)
Copied by Aito, Xpeng, Nio, BYD
MIIT bars new filings with the lamp (Jul 27-29)

entities.bio: Founded 2015, Beijing, by Li Xiang (李想, CEO). Public (NASDAQ: LI, HKEX: 2015). Premium EREV/EV maker; one of China's top-three premium NEV brands. Originated the now-industry-standard blue 'ADAS marker lamp' design on the L9 in August 2022.

entities.name: Pony.ai
entities.desc: US-listed Chinese AV company with dual business lines: robotaxi (commercial ops via GAC JV) and autonomous trucking. One of the first Chinese AV companies to achieve a US listing, giving it dollar-denominated access to capital. Positions as an asset-light, licensing-focused model by partnering with OEMs rather than owning large vehicle fleets directly. **Uber expansion to Europe/Middle East (Aug 14, 2026):** Pony.ai and Uber expanded their partnership to deploy 2,000+ robotaxis across Europe, growing from their existing Zagreb service — Europe's first commercial robotaxi launch, run with local fleet operator Verne — to four additional European cities plus a Middle East rollout; specific cities and timing undisclosed. The deal keeps Pony.ai's three-layer model intact (L4 driving stack + Uber demand platform + local fleet operator), extending its international footprint as Chinese AV exports face rising scrutiny in the US market.

tags.l: 2,000+ robotaxis planned for Europe + Middle East (Aug 14)
Builds on Zagreb launch — Europe's first commercial robotaxi service

entities.bio: Founded 2016, Guangzhou, by James Peng (彭军, CEO) and Lou Tiancheng (楼天城, CTO) — former Google and Baidu AI researchers. Listed NASDAQ (PONY) in 2024. Backed by Toyota (strategic), GAC (Chinese OEM JV partner), and CITIC.

entities.name: WeRide
entities.desc: Global-expansion-focused AV operator with commercial deployments in Abu Dhabi and Singapore alongside China. Differentiated by an international footprint: Abu Dhabi and Singapore deployments are revenue-generating, not just regulatory pilots. Autonomous bus operations run commercially in multiple cities. The international presence positions WeRide as the most globally distributed Chinese AV platform, reducing dependence on China's still-volatile robotaxi licensing environment.
entities.bio: Founded 2017, Guangzhou and San Jose (CA), by Tony Han (韩旭, CEO) — former NIO and Baidu self-driving engineer. Listed NASDAQ (WRD). Backed by Renault; operates commercial robotaxi and autonomous minibus services.

entities.name: Momenta
entities.desc: Data-driven AV company whose 'Flywheel' strategy uses each additional mile driven to generate training data, improving models that enable more miles. Cross-Pacific backing from Toyota AND GM gives Momenta OEM credibility rare among Chinese AV peers. **HK IPO (mid-2026):** Listed HKEX as 6880.HK with 14 cornerstone investors covering ~50% of offering — one of the most institutionally-anchored Chinese tech IPOs of 2026. The cross-Pacific investor base signals that data-driven AV infrastructure is perceived as less geopolitically sensitive than frontier LLMs.
entities.bio: Founded 2016, Beijing, by Cao Xu (曹旭, CEO) — former Microsoft Research Asia and Google DeepMind researcher. Private; backed by Toyota, GM, Mercedes-Benz (cornerstone), BYD's Golden Link, and GIC (Singapore). Listed HKEX (6880.HK) mid-2026.

entities.name: Huawei Smart Car
entities.desc: China's 'Bosch of autonomous driving' — provides ADS as a Tier-1 supplier to OEMs rather than building vehicles. Core partners: Seres/AITO, CHERY/Luxeed. Strategy: own the AI brain (perception, planning, decision) while OEM partners own vehicle hardware and distribution. Huawei's ADS is widely considered the most capable ADAS system in China across its partner vehicle lineup. ByteDance competes via Volcengine as an alternative AI cloud platform for smart factories (Seres partnership, Jun 2026) — a rare OEM loyalty contest between China's two dominant tech ecosystems.
entities.bio: Huawei Intelligent Automotive Solution (HIAS) is a business unit of Huawei Technologies (founded 1987, Shenzhen, by Ren Zhengfei). Operates as a Tier-1 automotive AI supplier rather than an OEM, partnering with automakers including Seres (AITO brand) and CHERY (Luxeed).

entities.name: MIIT
entities.desc: Ministry of Industry & Information Technology. Regulates AI, telecoms, semiconductors. Developing national agentic AI security standards in response to OpenClaw wave. Administers HEIS digital identity platform for humanoid robots. **Humanoid census (July 20, 2026 / Issue #63):** MIIT data release: China has developed 400+ humanoid robot products, more than half the global total; Chinese quadruped robots account for close to 70% of global sales. Same-day state data put China's daily AI token consumption at 140 trillion, up more than 1,000-fold since early 2024. Follows the July WAIC statement that 2026 humanoid output should exceed 100,000 units. Product-count and unit-volume metrics measure breadth, not revenue — monetization remains concentrated in a handful of vendors (Unitree: RMB 1.7B revenue, RMB 591M adjusted profit in 2025). **Blue ADAS light ban (July 27–29, 2026 / Issue #73):** MIIT moved to strictly enforce the existing GB4785-2019 vehicle-lighting standard, which limits exterior lights to white, red, yellow and amber, effectively banning the blue 'Automated Driving System Marker Lamps' that OEMs (starting with Li Auto's L9 in 2022, followed by Aito, Xpeng, Nio and BYD) have used to signal when ADAS is active. New passenger-vehicle regulatory filings featuring the lamps will be barred starting with next month's filing cycle; the National Automotive Standardisation Committee is expected to issue supplementary clarifying requirements. Automakers are still working out remediation for already-sold vehicles — OTA updates to change lamp color or disable the feature are one option under discussion. The lamps had sat in a regulatory grey area for four years despite technically violating the 2019 standard; it is unclear why enforcement came now rather than sooner. **Mandatory autonomous-driving safety standard (Aug 4, 2026 / Issue #78):** Released, jointly with the State Administration for Market Regulation and National Standardization Administration, China's first mandatory national standard (强制性国家标准) for L3/L4 autonomous driving system safety — effective July 1, 2027. Applies to M/N-category vehicles (not automated parking); requires lifecycle safety-assurance processes, simulation/closed-track/road testing, an automated-driving 'black box' data recorder, and continuous driver-readiness monitoring for L3 systems. Replaces a city-by-city pilot patchwork (Beijing, Shenzhen, Wuhan, Hangzhou) with one national bar, landing as Goldman Sachs raises its 2026 China robotaxi fleet estimate to ~14,000 vehicles (2030: 700,000+). MIIT signaled further tightening of market-access management and testing methods to come — this is a first step, not a finished framework. **Embodied-AI infrastructure census (Aug 21, 2026 / Issue #97):** Report released alongside the 2026 World Robot Conference shows more than 70 embodied-AI training grounds operational nationwide as of end-June, with another 46 under construction or in planning. China shipped over 40,000 humanoid robots in H1 2026 — about 97% of global shipments on the cited figure — building on the July count of 400+ complete humanoid products. The shipment and training-ground counts describe manufacturing and infrastructure breadth, not deployment economics or unit profitability; MIIT's own framing (products developed, training grounds built) does not distinguish pilot deployments from revenue-generating placements.

tags.l: Daily AI token calls: 140T, +1,000x since early 2024
First mandatory AV safety standard, eff. Jul 2027
Hits Li Auto, Aito, Xpeng, Nio, BYD designs

entities.name: CAC
entities.zh: 国家互联网信息办公室
entities.desc: Cyberspace Administration of China. Regulates generative AI, data, online content. Co-issued first AI agent (智能体) regulations jointly with NDRC and MIIT on May 8, 2026.

entities.name: NDRC
entities.zh: 国家发展和改革委员会
entities.desc: **AI capital controls and M&A oversight.** Ordered leading AI startups to reduce US LP capital exposure and reject US-origin capital without clearance (2026). Codified a technology-tracing approach to outbound investment review — effectively blocking Meta's acquisition of Manus. Sets the regulatory frame under which offshore listings, cross-border AI investment, and foreign LP participation in Chinese AI funds are evaluated. **Compute rationing rule (Jul 2026).** With MIIT and the National Data Bureau, issued guidance barring small data-center builds (under ¥300M / 1,000 racks / 2,500 kW) by local govts and SOEs, requiring pre-approval for medium projects, and confining large clusters to national hubs — with subsidy and grid-access penalties for non-compliant builds. Marks a pivot from the 2022 東数西算 buildout push to central rationing, prompted by sub-30% utilization at some AI compute centers. **Fiscal instruments and AI agent rules.** Accelerated deployment of ¥800B in policy financial instruments (Q3 2026) with compute buildout cited as a ¥4T private-investment lever over the 15th Five-Year Plan. Co-issued first AI agent (智能体) regulations with CAC and MIIT (May 8, 2026).

entities.name: State Council
entities.desc: China's chief administrative authority, chaired by Premier Li Qiang (李强). Convenes the State Council executive meeting (国务院常务会议), the venue where cross-ministry economic directives are formally adopted before implementation by NDRC, MOF, PBOC and other ministries. **Enterprise-arrears crackdown (Aug 21, 2026 / Issue #97):** Executive meeting deployed a stepped-up campaign to clear overdue payments owed to enterprises (清理拖欠企业账款), explicitly targeting large companies — including state-owned enterprises — that are slow to pay small and medium-sized suppliers. Directed local governments to use special bonds (专项债券) and specialized central-bank relending (专项再贷款) to fund catch-up payments, called for industry-specific standard payment terms (账期), tighter disclosure of large-enterprise payment behavior, and clearer criteria for labeling arrears as bad-faith conduct. Same meeting reviewed next-generation telecom network buildout and air-quality work. The directive is a policy signal about private-sector cash-flow stress rather than a fiscal transfer itself — actual relief depends on how quickly local governments draw down the bond/relending tools and how the new disclosure rules are enforced against large payers.

tags.l: Targets large-enterprise, SOE payment delays to SMEs
Special bonds + relending to fund catch-up
Signal of SME cash-flow stress, not direct transfer

entities.name: MOST
entities.desc: Ministry of Science & Technology. Funds basic R&D and national AI programs. Key allocator of state research grants for AI, semiconductor, and quantum computing.

entities.name: Huawei Ascend 950
entities.desc: Next-gen Huawei AI training platform: triggered a $5.6B ByteDance order — the largest known single AI chip purchase in China; targeting 750K units in 2026. DeepSeek's native V4 optimization for Ascend 950 cemented Huawei as the default domestic training platform, with Beijing directing major cloud providers to defer Nvidia H200 deployment to protect the Huawei ecosystem. Part of a $12B Huawei AI chip revenue target for 2026. Sits alongside the 910C (volume inference, 600K units) in the Ascend family — 950 is for frontier training, 910C for volume deployment.
entities.bio: Next-generation AI training chip from Huawei Technologies (华为). Designated internally as Ascend 950PR. Designed by Huawei, manufactured at SMIC's enhanced 7nm process. First chip for which DeepSeek V4 was natively optimized.

entities.name: Zhongji Innolight
entities.desc: Critical Nvidia infrastructure vendor: high-speed optical interconnects linking GPU clusters inside AI datacenters. Top-weighted CSI 300 constituent at 5.3% in June 2026 (displacing CATL and Kweichow Moutai) — clearest barometer of AI datacenter capex sentiment in China's equity market. Q1 2026: revenue +192% YoY, profit +262% YoY. Demand structurally tied to each new hyperscaler infrastructure buildout wave; Nvidia's AI datacenter revenue directly converts to Zhongji Innolight orders for 400G/800G optical transceivers. The July 28 chip-sector selloff (-15.69%) reflected fears of AI infrastructure circular funding rather than Zhongji's fundamentals.
entities.bio: Founded 2003, Shenzhen; listed SZSE (300308). CEO: Liu Ren (刘人). World's largest maker of high-speed optical transceiver modules; primary Nvidia supplier for AI datacenter optical interconnects. Q1 2026 revenue ¥19.5B (+192% YoY); net profit ¥5.73B (+262% YoY).

entities.name: LineShine
entities.desc: China's #1 supercomputer and TOP500 leader as of June 23, 2026: 2.19 exaflop Linpack benchmark — 22% faster than the US El Capitan; China's first TOP500 top position since Sunway TaihuLight (2017). ~14M processing cores on domestic Arm-based CPU designs; zero Nvidia or AMD GPUs; custom interconnects. **Strategic significance:** LineShine proves China's domestic chip ecosystem achieves world-class HPC benchmarks without Western silicon. It does NOT close the AI training gap — H100/B200-class Nvidia hardware still leads on AI-specific workloads — but crosses the HPC benchmark threshold considered out of reach five years ago.
entities.bio: LineShine (灵晟) is a state-built national supercomputer operated by the National Supercomputing Center in Shenzhen (深圳国家超级计算中心). Not a company — a national infrastructure asset. Achieved #1 on the TOP500 list in June 2026.

entities.name: BYD Robotics
entities.desc: BYD's robotics division leverages parent's unmatched manufacturing scale, vertical integration (battery, electronics, assembly), and 400K+ global dealer network as potential humanoid distribution infrastructure. Strategy: proprietary hardware (Xiao Di humanoid, debuted Aug 2026) plus an open platform for other robot makers to procure BYD components. BYD has previously pilot-deployed Unitree and UBTECH humanoids in its own factories as an internal reference. The key competitive moat is cost: BYD's manufacturing infrastructure should allow it to produce robots at a structural cost advantage over pure-play robotics startups.
entities.bio: BYD Robotics (比亚迪机器人) is an internal division of BYD Co., Ltd. (HKEX: 1211 / SZSE: 002594, founded 1995, Shenzhen, by Wang Chuanfu). Confirmed June 4, 2026. Strategy: proprietary humanoid hardware + open platform to supply other robotics companies.

entities.name: Galbot
entities.desc: Top-tier Beijing embodied AI company developing general-purpose humanoid robots for service and industrial applications. Wang He's academic pedigree (PKU/Stanford) combined with an investor base spanning internet (Meituan), battery (CATL), automotive (BAIC, SAIC), and AI (SenseTime) gives Galbot broad industry distribution optionality. Specifically named in Alibaba's competitive peer-set analysis for its Qwen Robot Suite launch. $1B+ raised is among the largest humanoid funding totals in China; HK IPO in process.
entities.bio: Founded May 2023, Beijing, by Wang He (王鹤, CEO) — Peking University professor and former Stanford AI Lab researcher. Private; backed by Meituan, IDG Capital, CATL, BAIC, SenseTime, SAIC, and China's National AI Fund. Raised $1B+; HK IPO in process.

entities.name: ModelBest
entities.desc: Developer of efficient language models with an early-mover position in domestic chip training. **BitCPM-CANN and LongCat-2.0-Preview:** Among the first five Chinese AI models confirmed using Huawei Ascend (CANN software stack) for pre-training or post-training as of June 2026 — an early example of the training-phase domestic chip adoption now becoming mainstream. The CANN suffix in model names signals native Ascend optimization, part of Huawei's strategy to build model-level lock-in alongside chip hardware.
entities.bio: Chinese AI research lab focused on efficient language models. Specific founding details and team are not publicly disclosed as of mid-2026. Private. Developer of the BitCPM and LongCat model families, among the first models trained on Huawei Ascend (CANN software stack).

entities.name: Seres
entities.desc: Chongqing EV manufacturer best known for the AITO brand powered by Huawei's ADAS system. **Xiaosai humanoid (Jun 2026):** Two models deployed in Seres' smart factory: Xiaosai 01 (chassis assembly quality inspection) and Xiaosai 02 (exterior vehicle configuration check). Strategic partner: ByteDance Volcengine (signed Oct 2024) provides multimodal cloud-edge AI for robot decision-making — a notable example of ByteDance AI powering factory robots in a Huawei-partnered OEM ecosystem.
entities.bio: Founded 2016, Chongqing, initially as a US-China EV venture; listed SZSE (601127). Best known for the AITO brand (co-developed with Huawei Smart Car). Entered humanoid robotics June 2026 with the Xiaosai (小赛) robot family — already deployed in its Chongqing smart factory.

entities.name: Kunlunxing Robotics
entities.desc: Fastest 0-to-unicorn in China's embodied AI sector: three funding rounds in 90 days from March 2026 founding, raising a cumulative several billion yuan ($275M). **Kunlun World Model (昆仑世界模型):** Dual-system architecture (high-level reasoning + low-level motion controller); full-stack proprietary hardware. Pre-product as of June 2026 — the funding is entirely on founder pedigree (Alibaba Cloud, Li Auto AV, Huawei backgrounds). The speed of capital formation ($275M before a product line) reflects the structural feature of China's embodied AI market in 2026: institutional capital reserving positions independent of product milestones.
entities.bio: Founded March 2026, Beijing, by Ren Geng (任耕, CEO) — former President of Alibaba Cloud China and Huawei overseas country CEO — and Lang Xianpeng — former President of Autonomous Driving at Li Auto. Raised $275M in 3 rounds within 90 days. Investors: Gaorong Capital, GL Ventures, CAS Star, Sinovation, C&D Capital.

entities.name: Anyverse Dynamics
entities.desc: Embodied AI software platform developing 'general-purpose brains' for robots — targeting industrial manufacturing, energy, and retail clients. **Hyperspeed funding (H1 2026):** Angel round >$200M led by a JD.com-affiliated fund, C Capital, Hony Capital, and HongShan/Linear Capital; total H1 2026 fundraising in the several-hundred-million dollar range. One of the most capital-intensive pre-product embodied AI raises globally. **Software-layer bet:** 140+ domestic humanoid competitors implies early price-war risk before consolidation; Anyverse's thesis is that the software/intelligence layer — not hardware — will be the margin-capture layer once hardware commoditizes.
entities.bio: Founded 2025, Beijing, by Zhang Yufeng (张玉峰, CEO) — former Vice President of Horizon Robotics — along with Xia Zhongpu and Wenda Xu from autonomous driving and intelligent mobility backgrounds. Raised $200M+ in angel round (June 2026); pre-Series A of similar size nearly complete.

entities.name: Booster Robotics
entities.desc: Full-size bipedal humanoid robot developer focused on dynamic mobility. T1 won first place in both the Speed Competition and the Obstacle Avoidance & Door Opening Challenge at IEEE-RAS Humanoids 2024 (Nancy, France, November 2024). MWC Shanghai 2026 finalist in the GSMA Humanoid Robot Football Penalties Challenge. The competition-circuit strategy reflects a model of using tournaments as scaled real-world testing infrastructure to rapidly iterate mobility models. Smaller funding base than peers but demonstrated dynamic performance credentials.
entities.bio: Founded 2023, Beijing, by Cheng Hao (程昊, CEO) — Tsinghua University master's graduate in the Department of Automation. Backed by Source Code Capital, Tsinghua Innovation Ventures, and GreenHarbor Investment; raised ~$27.9M across three rounds. Products: T1 full-size bipedal humanoid.

entities.name: NAURA Technology
entities.desc: China's leading domestic semiconductor equipment maker — a critical node in reducing dependence on ASML, Applied Materials, and Lam Research. **CXMT capex beneficiary:** CXMT's ¥66.6B STAR Market IPO (July 2026) will drive multi-year equipment procurement cycles that NAURA is positioned to capture as China's preferred domestic supplier. Each DRAM fab build (CXMT adding capacity in Beijing, Shanghai, Hefei; YMTC expanding) is a visible forward pipeline for NAURA. The equipment-maker business model has longer lead times than chip designers but more durable revenue visibility once fab commitments are placed.
entities.bio: Founded 1998 (predecessor), Beijing. Listed SZSE (002371). CEO: Feng Guoping (冯国平). China's largest domestic semiconductor equipment manufacturer; key product lines: CVD, PVD, etch, thermal processing, and cleaning equipment for wafer fabs.

entities.name: AMEC
entities.desc: Advanced semiconductor etch equipment maker — the most internationally credible Chinese equipment company in advanced-node tooling. **Samsung/SK Hynix evaluation (Aug 5, 2026):** Reuters reported both South Korean memory makers tested AMEC etch tools for China-based fabs; both companies denied the reporting — claim remains contested. **H1 2026 results (Aug 3):** Net profit +282–311% y/y to ¥2.7–2.9B — but ~2/3 from fair-value gains on CXMT equity stakes, not equipment sales. Core adjusted profit +86–123% y/y on revenue +34.9% to ¥6.69B. CEO acknowledged on CCTV that Chinese customers still default to foreign tools 'out of habit.' TSMC reportedly phasing Chinese-made equipment out of its most advanced fabs — a ceiling on AMEC's addressable market abroad.
