H1 profit +282-311%, but 2/3 is investment gains (Aug 3)
TSMC reportedly phasing out Chinese tools

entities.bio: Founded 2004, Shanghai, by Gerald Yin (尹志尧, CEO) — former Applied Materials Distinguished Member of Technical Staff. Listed SSE STAR Market (688012). Products: plasma etch and CVD deposition equipment; one of the few Chinese companies with etch tools competitive at advanced nodes.

entities.name: Shanghai Yuliangsheng Technology
entities.desc: China's first domestic immersion DUV lithography tool maker. **DUV breakthrough (Jul 2026):** Began mass-producing China's first homegrown immersion DUV tools — SMIC testing since September 2025 with encouraging results. 2026 plan: ~5 units (targeting SMIC, Hua Hong, CXMT); 2027: ~20 units. Tools target mature (~28nm) nodes but can reach ~7nm via multi-patterning exposure. Contrast: ASML delivered 131 immersion systems last year. News triggered a July 27 selloff in ASML and the Philadelphia SOX. Mostly domestic components; some key parts still imported from Japan. The US Congress's bipartisan Match Act would tighten controls on immersion DUV tools if enacted.

tags.l: Match Act would tighten US controls

entities.bio: Founded July 2022, Shanghai, with Liu Jun as legal representative. State-backed lithography equipment startup assembled under Huawei's coordination, combining DUV R&D teams from multiple Chinese firms following the US 2022 advanced-chip-tool export controls. Primary focus: developing domestic immersion deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography tools.

entities.name: CaoCao Inc.
entities.desc: Geely's primary robotaxi commercialization platform. **Driverless testing (Jul 27, 2026):** First company in Hangzhou approved for safety-driver-free road testing (April 2026 approval); launched fully driverless robotaxi testing in Hangzhou's Binjiang District Jul 27 — the most aggressive step among Chinese robotaxi peers following the lifting of the April 2026 license freeze. Uses end-to-end large-model architecture. **Eva Cab:** China's first ground-up purpose-built robotaxi platform, targeting 2027 mass production. Also runs the world's first 'Green Intelligent Mobility Hub' in Hangzhou (automated battery swapping, cleaning, prep for a ~100-vehicle fleet).

tags.l: First driverless (no safety driver) test post-freeze
Post Baidu Apollo Go Wuhan stall / license freeze

entities.bio: Founded May 2015, Hangzhou, as the ride-hailing arm of Geely Holding Group (founded 1986 by Li Shufu). CEO: Gong Xin; Chairman: Zhou Hang. Listed HKEX June 25, 2026. Second-largest ride-hailing platform in China (5.4% market share) behind Didi (70%+); operates across 136 cities.

entities.name: DJI
entities.desc: World's largest consumer and commercial drone maker — Phantom, Mavic, Agras (agricultural), and Matrice (industrial) series. Estimated 70%+ global market share in consumer drones. **CAAC Airworthiness Regime (Jul 1, 2026):** China's first binding statutory drone framework took effect — manufacturers must hold CAAC airworthiness certificates and engrave unique IDs on each unit. DJI's scale and compliance infrastructure give it an advantage over smaller competitors under the new regime. US Entity List restrictions limit US component sourcing and US distribution, but DJI has largely replaced US-sourced components since the 2020 designation.
entities.bio: Founded 2006, Shenzhen, by Wang Tao (汪滔, Frank Wang, CEO) — a Hong Kong University of Science and Technology robotics graduate. Private; principally founder-controlled. On US Entity List since 2020 and US DoD 'Chinese Military Company' list since 2022.

entities.name: EHang
entities.desc: Leading eVTOL manufacturer; received China's first civil type certificate from CAAC in 2023 — a regulatory milestone ahead of global competitors. EH216-S is a two-seat passenger AAV for short urban hops and tourism. **CAAC Airworthiness Regime (Jul 1, 2026):** New mandatory certification framework benefits EHang as an early mover with an existing type certificate — the certification moat may take years for entrants to replicate. China's government has designated the '低空经济' (low-altitude economy) as a strategic growth sector projected at ¥2T+ by 2030; EHang is the best-positioned listed Chinese eVTOL company, though commercialization timeline remains uncertain.
entities.bio: Founded 2014, Guangzhou, by Hu Huazhi (胡华智, CEO). Listed NASDAQ (EH). EH216-S received China's first civil aircraft type certificate from CAAC in 2023 — the world's first type-certified passenger autonomous aerial vehicle.

entities.name: Meituan
entities.desc: China's #1 food delivery and local-services platform. Not a pure AI play, but committed to frontier AI: **LongCat-2.0 (Jul 2026):** 1.6T-parameter MoE model trained on ~50,000 domestic accelerators — first publicly claimed trillion-parameter pretraining run on non-Nvidia silicon; inference confirmed on Ascend, Moore Threads, and MetaX. **Humanoid ecosystem investor:** Meituan's Long-Z Investments participated in Galaxea AI, Galbot, Guangdong Tianji, Unitree Robotics, and Zeroth — positioning Meituan's delivery and local-services infrastructure for eventual robotics distribution. CEO Wang Xing has framed AI as a 'must-answer question' for Meituan's competitive position.
entities.bio: Founded 2010, Beijing, by Wang Xing (王兴, CEO) — a serial internet entrepreneur and co-founder of Xiaonei (China's Facebook). Listed HKEX (3690). China's dominant food delivery and local-services super-app; 700M+ registered users.

entities.name: Zeroth
entities.desc: Home-focused humanoid and companion robot maker targeting consumer markets before factory deployment. Products: M1 (small humanoid), W1 (tracked robot), Jupiter (full-size home companion), N1 (collaborative heterogeneous-arm system). **Commercial traction:** 30,000+ orders; 600% revenue growth YoY H1 2026 — an unusually strong commercial signal for a young consumer robotics company. Ant + Geely + gaming publisher (37 Interactive) cap table suggests strategic distribution intent. **Regulatory risk:** Embodied companion robots sit close to the CAC's new anthropomorphic-AI rules (Jul 2026) that forced Qwen and Doubao companion agents offline — a regulatory overhang that didn't exist when the company was founded.
entities.bio: Founded 2022/2023, Suzhou, connected to Suzhou JoyIn Intelligent Technology. Home-focused embodied AI startup. Pre-Series A led by Ant Group (¥500M); total ~$147M raised. Investors: Ant Group, Geely Capital, 37 Interactive Entertainment, Hua Capital.

entities.name: DexForce
entities.desc: Embodied AI platform company — NOT a robot maker. DexVerse platform spans synthetic data generation, 3D perception, skill/task generation, and model training; deployed in industrial cells for inspection, picking, and dexterous manipulation. ¥100M H1 2026 revenue; targeting ¥300M+ full year. **State-capital model:** With US LP capital screened out by NDRC requirements, DexForce is funded wholly by a state-capital syndicate — a patient but political investor base that selects for SOE procurement pipelines over consumer stories. Contrasts with Morphi (same ¥1B scale, platform-capital from Alibaba/Tencent on founder pedigree).
entities.bio: Founded 2021, Shenzhen, by a team with backgrounds in industrial automation and AI. Private; Series B ¥1B (~$143M) at ¥10B+ valuation (2026), funded entirely by state-linked capital: Shenzhen Capital Group, Qianhai Fund of Funds, Hengjian Asset Management, ICBC Capital.

entities.name: Dongfang Suanxin
entities.desc: 3D near-memory computing (近存计算) chip startup addressing the memory-bandwidth wall that constrains domestic AI accelerators. **DF1000 chip (WAIC Jul 2026):** 14nm AI chip claiming 520 teraflops BF16 performance using 3D-stacked near-memory architecture — designed to bypass both HBM requirements and standard compute paradigms. Mass production expected by end of 2026. WAIC 2026 debut was spotlighted alongside Huawei's Atlas 950 SuperPoD and StepFun's agent OS — China's first significant state-platform endorsement. If the performance claims hold at scale, it represents a credible alternative architecture to Nvidia's conventional GPU + HBM design.
entities.bio: Founded 2024, Shanghai, by Wei Shaojun (魏少军, CEO) — Tsinghua University professor and Vice President of the China Semiconductor Industry Association. Backed by state funds, Meituan, Xiaomi, and JD.com; valuation RMB 12.3B. Core product: 3D near-memory computing AI chips.

entities.name: Nexchip Semiconductor
entities.desc: Mature-node wafer foundry (display drivers, CMOS image sensors, power management, microcontrollers) — the high-volume end of semiconductors enabling China's consumer electronics supply chain. **HK IPO (Jul 10, 2026):** Raised HK$6.98B ($891M) at top of range; +14% Day 1; 57% discount to A-share close — continues the pattern of Chinese semiconductor companies using HK as a capital channel alongside STAR listings. **Phase IV fab:** ¥35.5B investment for 55,000 wafers/month at 28/40nm; equipment move-in end Q2 2026; full capacity Q2 2028. Risk: mature-node overcapacity building across China — anti-involution pricing dynamics could hit display-driver and image-sensor pricing.
entities.bio: Founded 2015, Hefei, as a joint venture between Hefei city government and Taiwan's Powerchip Semiconductor (力晶). Chairman: Cai Guozhi (Tsai Kuo-Chih); CEO: Tsai Hui-Chia. China's 3rd-largest wafer foundry after SMIC and Hua Hong. Dual-listed: STAR Market (688249) and HKEX (July 2026, raised $891M).

entities.name: Morphi
entities.desc: Embodied intelligence startup with no product launched as of August 2026. **Record ¥1B+ angel round (Jul 2026):** China's largest first institutional round in embodied AI — Alibaba + Tencent co-led (a rare joint strategic check from the two largest internet rivals). Investment thesis: Huawei's data-flywheel approach (iterative real-world interaction → better models), applied by its architect (CTO Huang Qing) to general robotics. Industry estimates put all usable real-robot interaction data globally at ~500,000 hours — the scarcity Morphi must solve. The ¥7B+ valuation before a product line sets an ambitious benchmark; Alibaba/Tencent co-investment is itself a market signal about how both companies view the embodied AI software opportunity.
entities.bio: Founded 2025, Beijing, by Gao Wenli (高文力, CEO) — co-founder of cross-border logistics firm iMile — and Huang Qing (黄青, CTO) — former head of Huawei's autonomous driving AI division who oversaw ADS from 1.0 to 4.0 and pioneered end-to-end architecture commercialization. Alibaba and Tencent co-led the ¥1B+ angel round; valuation >¥7B.

entities.name: LimX Dynamics
entities.desc: General-purpose humanoid robot developer. **'Big brain / small brain' architecture (大脑小脑):** Whole-body motion foundation model + VLA action layer + LLM-driven embodied agent OS — a tiered intelligence design for flexible deployment. **Overseas sales:** Majority of robot orders from overseas (Middle East, Europe, Asia) with thousands of units placed — unusual for a company at LimX's funding stage. Stone Venture (UAE) consecutive follow-ons represent the Gulf sovereign capital wave substituting for US LP money restricted by NDRC. Pre-IPO label (Jul 2026) commits to a public listing without specifying venue or timeline.
entities.bio: Founded 2021, Shenzhen. Private; pre-IPO round ~$200M (Jul 2026), totaling ~$400M raised in 6 months. UAE-based Stone Venture made consecutive follow-on investments — Gulf sovereign-adjacent capital substituting for US LP money restricted by the NDRC framework.

entities.name: NBS
entities.desc: National Bureau of Statistics — China's official data agency; publishes GDP, retail sales, industrial output, fixed asset investment, CPI/PPI. Q2 2026 GDP released July 15, 2026: +4.3% YoY, slowest since Q4 2022 and first quarter below the 4.5–5.0% target band since Covid. June retail +1.0% YoY with autos −16.1%; exports carried industrial output. Late-July Politburo is the policy-response venue to watch. **June 70-city home prices (released July 15–16, 2026 / Issue #59):** New-home prices -3.3% y/y (36th consecutive annual decline, mildest since Feb 2026), -0.15% m/m vs -0.2% in May. Cities with m/m gains rose to 20 (from 16 in May) — most since May 2025. Shanghai new homes +3.1% y/y, the standout. Second-hand prices -0.32% m/m, worst in four months; first-tier second-hand -4.9% y/y. Credit backdrop: outstanding bank loan growth slowed a 15th straight month to 5.2% y/y with household borrowing weak — stabilization signal in new-home prices not yet confirmed by secondary market or credit demand. **H1 industrial profits: 18.7% headline, concentrated in computing gear (July 27, 2026 / Issue #72):** Profits at above-scale industrial firms (规模以上工业企业) rose 18.7% y/y to ¥3.95T ($583.3B) in H1 2026; June growth decelerated to 15.1% from 21.1% in May. Distribution highly uneven: electronics-sector profits +96.9% y/y (computer manufacturing +689.3%, computer peripherals +305.8%), while auto manufacturing profits fell 19.5% as vehicle sales declined for a ninth straight month. Reads as consistent with the Jul 28 chip-sector selloff (Issue #71) from the other direction — a large share of headline industrial profit growth looks like AI-infrastructure capex (servers, computing peripherals) rather than broad-based domestic demand recovery, leaving industrial-profit data more exposed to AI capex cycles than aggregate GDP/PMI suggests. **July manufacturing PMI contracts (released July 31, 2026 / Issue #74):** Official Manufacturing PMI fell to 49.2 from 50.3 in June, missing consensus (50.0) and marking the first sub-50 reading since February — a 1.1-point drop. New orders fell to 48.5, the lowest since 2023, from 51.2; production fell to 49.9 from 51.4; new export orders returned to contraction at 49.0 from 50.1. Officials and analysts cited weak domestic and external demand, elevated input costs, and typhoon disruption to coastal production. The reading landed the day the Politburo (#73) pledged 'incremental' fiscal and monetary support for H2 — the PMI miss is the data backdrop to that readout, not a separate policy response. The new-orders collapse is the more diagnostic figure than the headline miss: it points to a demand problem rather than a one-off supply disruption, though one month of data with a genuine typhoon effect complicates reading trend versus noise. **July CPI/PPI: inflation still shallow, factory-gate deflation persists (released Aug 9, 2026 / Issue #83):** CPI rose 0.5% y/y in July (core CPI, ex food/energy, +0.9% y/y) but fell 0.1% m/m; PPI rose 3.5% y/y — decelerating from June's 4.1% and missing the 3.8% consensus — while falling 0.7% m/m. Weaker energy prices and soft demand drove the miss. The data lands a week after PBOC's pledge to keep monetary policy 'appropriately loose' through 2H2026 and ahead of the Politburo meeting later in August where investors expect more targeted stimulus; the PPI miss keeps pressure on Beijing's anti-involution (反内卷, fǎn nèijuǎn) campaign against destructive price competition, which has yet to show up as a durable reflation signal in the factory-gate data. **July activity data confirms broad-based slowdown (released Aug 17, 2026, briefing delayed to 3pm / Issue #90):** Industrial output rose 5.7% y/y, below the ~6% consensus and down from 6.8% in June. Retail sales grew 3.7% y/y, the weakest print of 2026 and short of the ~4.6% consensus, down from 4.8% in June. Property investment fell roughly 12% y/y over the first seven months; private fixed-asset investment is down 1.5% y/y year-to-date, the steepest decline since the pandemic-hit 2020 comparison. The survey-based urban unemployment rate ticked up to 5.2%, above the 5.1% consensus and up from 5.0% in May and June. Construction PMI had already fallen to a record low of 47.0 in July. Taken together with the July manufacturing PMI contraction (Issue #74) and the sub-target Q2 GDP print, this is the third consecutive data point confirming the slowdown is broad-based across production, consumption, investment, and the labor market rather than a single-quarter or single-indicator blip — raising the bar for the 'incremental' H2 stimulus the Politburo (#73) has signaled but not yet detailed. **July new-home prices: decline accelerates (released Aug 17, 2026 / Issue #91):** New-home prices across 70 cities fell 0.18% m/m, deeper than June's -0.15% m/m — the pace of decline is worsening, not stabilizing, reversing the tentative improvement flagged in the June print (Issue #59). Combined with property investment already down roughly 12% y/y over the first seven months (Issue #90), the price data suggests demand-side weakness has not yet responded to the supply-side investment pullback. Foreign capital is nonetheless probing the sector selectively — PAG injected fresh capital into several Wanda Plazas in June–July — a valuation-driven bet on distressed commercial assets that is distinct from, and does not yet signal a turn in, residential pricing.

entities.name: World AI Cooperation Organization (WAICO)
entities.zh: 世界人工智能合作组织
entities.desc: Proposed China-led international AI governance body, to be headquartered in Shanghai. Xi Jinping (习近平) used his first-ever WAIC keynote (opening ceremony, July 17, 2026, alongside UN Secretary-General Guterres, Kazakh President Tokayev, and Thai PM Anutin) to elevate the initiative — an institutional vehicle for the Global AI Governance Initiative, framed around rejecting technology monopolies, providing 'international public goods,' and Global South capacity building. Positioned as an alternative pole to Western-led AI governance frameworks. Charter, membership, and funding details not yet published.

entities.name: Swancor Qiyuan
entities.desc: Personal/consumer robot brand via the most high-profile backdoor-listing (借壳上市) play in China's robotics cycle — AgiBot's ecosystem effectively taking a public vehicle through a composites company. **Quester1 (WAIC, Jul 17, 2026):** Shape-shifting robot that auto-switches between wheeled-bipedal and quadruped modes on a single chassis ('transformer cross-morphology integrated architecture'); target use cases: home companionship, outdoor escort, smart filming. Q1 product (Dec 2025): 88cm, 15kg 'world's smallest full-body force-controlled humanoid' with open SDK/HDK. Strategy: define the 'personal robot' category before it matures. Parent Swancor's lightweight composite materials feed robot bodies — a rare vertical materials advantage.

tags.l: Quester1 shape-shifting robot debuted at WAIC Jul 17

entities.bio: Swancor Qiyuan is the personal robotics brand of Swancor Advanced Materials (上纬新材, STAR: 688585), whose controlling interest shifted in November 2025 to Zhiyuan-AgiBot-affiliated vehicles (Zhiyuan Hengyue ~29.99%). CEO Tian Hua is ex-Huawei (wireless and computing) and ex-AgiBot (ecosystem GM, chief supply officer). Launched the Qiyuan brand December 31, 2025.

entities.name: PBOC
entities.desc: **Monetary policy: prolonged hold, weakening transmission.** 'Moderately loose' (适度宽松) stance since Dec 2025 CEWC; 7-day reverse repo anchored at 1.4%; LPRs at record lows (1-year 3.0%, 5-year 3.5%) for 14+ consecutive months through mid-2026 with most economists pushing next cut to 2027. Credit transmission deteriorated sharply in H1 2026: new RMB loans fell 17% y/y to ¥10.7T and total social financing grew just 7.4% — slowest on record — despite record-low rates. ~86% of listed banks trade below a sustainable net interest margin, constraining further pass-through. **Yuan internationalization: structural push accelerating.** Panda bond (熊猫债) issuance rose 60%+ y/y to ¥160B in H1 2026 (Goldman: 'historic opportunity'); ≥6 Chinese banks added ~12 EM currencies to direct yuan settlement in 2026; offshore yuan at strongest level since 2023. 2026-2030 reform plan (Aug 10) anchors CIPS expansion, digital yuan development, and Shanghai/HK as international financial centers. Same day, PBOC named Deutsche Bank as RMB clearing bank for Frankfurt — the first such designation for a foreign bank in Europe — as SWIFT data showed RMB's global payments share rising to 3.1% (5th-ranked currency, up from 2.75%) and CIPS average daily settlement climbing to ~¥830B in June from ~¥680B in 2025. **H2 2026 posture: fiscal over monetary.** Aug 2 work meeting pledged 'timely' tool adjustment but no RRR/rate-cut commitment — signaling data-dependent stance. Real H2 easing burden has shifted to fiscal (NDRC ¥800B instrument acceleration), with PBOC in a supporting liquidity role. **Digital yuan network expansion (Aug 17):** PBOC authorized eight more banks as e-CNY (数字人民币) operators — three national joint-stock lenders (Ping An, Hengfeng, China Bohai) and five city commercial banks (Shanghai, Hangzhou, Huishang, Changsha, Guangxi Beibu Gulf) — bringing the total to 30 operators, up from 10 before an April 2026 batch added 12. Newly approved banks are connected to the central-side digital-currency system but customer-facing rollout follows only after each completes technical preparation, so the operator count is a capacity/infrastructure metric rather than an adoption one. The expansion is explicitly tied to the 2026-2030 five-year reform plan's digital-yuan priority, positioning e-CNY as infrastructure for the same cross-border settlement and RMB internationalization push evident in the CIPS and panda-bond data above — a slow, deliberate buildout rather than a retail-adoption inflection.

Customer rollout still pending per-bank readiness

entities.bio: China's central bank, headquartered in Beijing; Governor Pan Gongsheng (潘功胜). Sets monetary policy via 7-day reverse repo rate and LPR benchmarks. Oversees RMB policy, financial system stability, and yuan internationalization.

entities.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA)
entities.desc: China's foreign ministry — increasingly the public voice for Beijing's AI diplomacy (WAICO, open-source-as-public-good framing). **July 18, 2026 (Issue #61):** Assistant Foreign Minister Liu Bin (刘彬) used the WAIC stage to dismiss allegations by Anthropic and other US labs that Chinese developers illicitly 'distill' (蒸馏) outputs from frontier American models: 'Some countries hype up distillation.' The rebuttal, without naming the US, signals the extraction dispute has moved from lab-to-lab accusation to state-level talking point — relevant to how model-provenance claims get litigated in export-control and IP venues.

entities.name: SAFE
entities.desc: State Administration of Foreign Exchange — manages China's $3.2T+ FX reserves and capital-account controls; the data source of record for cross-border flows. **H1 2026 FX data (July 17, 2026 / Issue #61):** Newly signed corporate FX hedging (套期保值) contracts +40% y/y to nearly $1.4T; hedging ratio 35.3% of corporate FX transactions (+5.3pp) as the yuan appreciated ~3.5%. Record $2.9T bank FX settlement; $9.2T cross-border receipts/payments (+20%+). Reiterated 'risk-neutral' (风险中性) guidance against currency speculation while easing derivative access.

entities.name: Central Huijin
entities.desc: Domestic investment arm of China's sovereign wealth fund (CIC) and the anchor of the 'national team' (国家队) that buys equities to stabilize markets. July 2026: PBOC said it would provide relending to back Huijin purchases as state buyers — China Reform Holdings (国新) and China Chengtong (诚通) — deployed ≥¥60B (~$8.9B) from July 19 to halt a tech-led rout that took the STAR Market down ~25% from its July 1 high. Record inflows into tech ETFs followed. Relending-financed equity support blurs the monetary–fiscal boundary and is the mechanism to watch.

entities.name: CSRC
entities.desc: China Securities Regulatory Commission — securities and futures regulator, chaired by Wu Qing (吴清) since 2024. Runs IPO registration (approved Unitree in a record 73–104 days; CXMT's mega-IPO) and coordinates market-stabilization policy. July 2026: Wu pledged 'all efforts' to safeguard stability as the national team deployed ≥¥60B against a tech-led rout; formalized a 'stability-first' counter-cyclical framework in January 2026. **HK offshore CGB futures debut (Aug 3, 2026 / Issue #78):** Wu attended HKEX's listing ceremony for the world's first offshore Chinese government bond futures contract — a cash-settled, 5-year, ¥500,000-face-value product with a 22,000-contract net position cap — calling it 'a natural development' after meticulous cross-border preparation and framing Hong Kong as the 'bridgehead' (桥头堡) for offshore RMB. Cited foreign holdings of Chinese interbank bonds at ~¥3.2T ($474B), roughly 4x since 2017, up from a shelved 2017 CGB futures pilot. A 10-year contract may follow.

tags.l: Wu Qing 'all efforts' stability pledge Jul 2026
Gatekeeper of the AI/robotics IPO calendar

entities.name: MOFCOM
entities.desc: Ministry of Commerce — runs China's export-control regime and the three-tier technology export catalogue (prohibited / restricted / contract registration). July 2026: consulting Alibaba, ByteDance and Z.ai on adding AI model weights, training data and Chinese chip designs to the catalogue (FT Jul 21, Reuters-confirmed) — expanding the July 7 model-access talks into a full export-control package that mirrors Washington's own playbook. Chip-design controls would bar TSMC/Qualcomm from building on Chinese designs, forcing consolidation onto SMIC (7nm vs TSMC N2 — a 2-3x efficiency penalty near-term, a domestic-foundry bet long-term). Pre-decisional: no category assignment, no timeline. Precedent for tightening: NDRC's forced unwind of Meta's $2B Manus acquisition (Apr 2026) ended 'Singapore washing.' **AI sanctions response (July 27, 2026 / Issue #71):** Issued a statement warning of 'all necessary measures' if Washington sanctions Chinese AI firms over the Moonshot/Kimi K3 distillation accusations, calling the claims factually and legally unfounded and accusing the US of 'AI hegemonism' (AI霸权主义) and 'politicising and weaponising technology and economic issues.' First on-record MOFCOM response in the Moonshot sanctions dispute; lands days ahead of the planned Xi-Trump summit. **14 EU entities added to export control list (July 24–25, 2026 / Issue #72):** Added 14 EU entities to the export control list, barring Chinese exporters from supplying them dual-use items (两用物项) — including rare earths and permanent magnets — without special authorization. Follows a June 22 action against US rare-earth producers MP Materials and USA Rare Earth; coincides with a July 1 whistleblower mechanism rewarding tips on strategic-mineral export violations. IEA estimates a fully implemented curb regime could put $6.5T of downstream production at risk annually (US + Europe ~half the exposure). Reads as MOFCOM extending its own entity-list playbook — modeled on Washington's chip-sector approach — from the US to Europe. **Drone export curbs + 6 US entities added (August 5, 2026 / Issue #79):** Announced same-day countermeasures against the US, effective immediately: exports to the US of drones and their key parts, components and related technologies on China's Dual-Use Items Export Control List (两用物项出口管制清单) now require case-by-case strict review (逐案审查) and lose access to licensing facilitation measures, and six US entities were placed on China's countermeasure list for 'assisting and supporting' US sanctions. Response to two US actions: the FCC's ban on Chinese drone imports and DHS's addition of 43 Chinese companies to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act entity list. Case-by-case review is a slower, more discretionary chokepoint than an outright ban — mirrors the rare-earth licensing-friction playbook MOFCOM has used since 2023 rather than a hard cutoff.

entities.name: Beijing Municipal Bureau of Economy and Information Technology
entities.zh: 北京市经济和信息化局
entities.py: Běijīng Shì Jīngjì hé Xìnxīhuà Jú
entities.desc: Beijing's municipal industry-and-IT regulator and the executor of the capital's AI compute buildout. At a July 21, 2026 briefing it targeted adding 50,000 PFLOPS of intelligent computing power in H2 2026 — total capacity past 130,000 PFLOPS by year-end, after a 22,000-PFLOPS H1 addition lifted supply to 82,000 — and unveiled 'token economy' policies to accelerate AI adoption across industries. Also backing an open-source 'RISC-V + AI OS' ecosystem as a full-stack alternative to Arm and x86. Feeds Beijing's January 2026 target of 200,000 PFLOPS citywide by 2027 and its bid to be the national 'AI highland' (人工智能高地); in parallel it is imposing low-carbon retrofits and punitive power pricing on 40 data centers that exceed energy standards.

entities.name: Politburo
entities.desc: The Communist Party's 24-member top decision-making body, chaired by Xi Jinping; its April, July and December meetings set economic policy direction, with the July session fixing the tone for H2. The late-July 2026 meeting (expected week of July 27) is the policy venue inheriting Q2 GDP of 4.3% — the first sub-target quarter since Covid — a 14-month LPR hold, and the July state-led market rescue. Sell-side expects a firmer easing tone and faster fiscal execution tilted toward AI, quantum and advanced manufacturing rather than a large consumption package; watch readout language on 增量政策 (incremental policies), property 止跌回稳, and 反内卷 capacity discipline. **July meeting readout (July 30, 2026 / Issue #73):** The Politburo met July 30 and, per the Xinhua readout, pledged to 'fully leverage the effectiveness of existing policies and roll out practical and effective incremental measures (增量政策) in a timely manner,' committing to accelerate the pace of fiscal spending and the use of bond proceeds alongside a 'moderately accommodative' monetary stance — but announced no explicit rate cut and gave few concrete new deliverables, matching most economists' 'supportive tone, light on specifics' expectations rather than a big-bang package. The bureau also set the fifth plenary session of the Central Committee for October 2026 — significant as the session a year ahead of the next Party Congress, where a major leadership reshuffle and a potential fourth term for Xi are in view. Markets showed limited immediate reaction: the readout landed roughly 30 minutes before the Shanghai close and was overshadowed by a same-day tech-stock rout (STAR 50 -5.4%) driven by valuation/positioning concerns, not the policy statement. H1 2026 GDP growth was 4.7%, still within the government's 4.5-5.0% full-year target band despite Q2's deceleration.

entities.desc: Chinese humanoid robotics company in the current embodied AI funding wave. PIA Automation (parent entity, now renamed PIABOT) announced a new embodied AI and humanoid robotics business segment in April 2026, including a JV with AgiBot called Joybot Manufacture to industrialize humanoid systems. Represents the factory automation tier of companies pivoting toward humanoid robots as the sector attracts institutional capital.
entities.bio: PIABOT Robotics is a Chinese humanoid robot maker in the 2024–2026 wave. Related to PIA Automation (now renamed PIABOT). A JV called Joybot Manufacture (with AgiBot) was established to industrialize humanoid systems for factory deployment.

entities.name: Ministry of Finance
entities.desc: China's fiscal authority — sets the deficit, manages central and local government bond programs, and co-approves local special-purpose bond (专项债券) projects with the NDRC. At a July 22, 2026 briefing, deputy DG of debt management Zhao Zeyong said H1 new SPB issuance reached ¥2.07T (47% of the annual quota), with >¥170B deployed as project capital and implicit debt (隐性债务) replacement proceeding. The 'self-review, self-issuance' (自审自发) pilot — provinces approving their own project lists without NDRC/MOF sign-off — expanded to Hebei, Jiangxi, Hubei and Chongqing; pilot regions accounted for ¥1.6T, 77% of national issuance. Government-managed fund revenue fell 21.6% y/y in H1, the land-sale channel still shrinking. **Interest-subsidy program expanded (Aug 21, 2026):** Vice Minister of Finance Liao Min (廖岷) disclosed a new package expanding the interest-subsidy scheme (贴息政策, tiēxī zhèngcè) for consumption loans: the personal consumption-loan subsidy ceiling rose from ¥3,000 to ¥5,000 per borrower, new credit-card installment purchases (autos, home renovation) became eligible, and the parallel service-sector business loan subsidy — originally covering catering, eldercare, tourism and six other categories — expanded to digital, green and retail sectors, with the per-borrower loan cap raised from ¥1M to ¥10M and the subsidy cap raised to ¥100,000. MOF separately disclosed ¥187.5B already deployed under the consumer-goods trade-in program (以旧换新, yǐ jiù huàn xīn), generating 178 million purchases worth ~¥1.32T, plus >¥370B in sales driven by invoice-lottery campaigns (发票摇奖) across 50 pilot cities.

tags.l: 自审自发 decentralization pilot expanding

entities.name: National Data Bureau
entities.desc: China's National Data Bureau (NDB), established 2023 under the NDRC to coordinate data-element markets, data infrastructure and national computing-power policy. In July 2026 it co-issued — with the NDRC and MIIT — guidance rationing data-center construction: barring small local-government/SOE builds, requiring pre-approval for medium projects, and confining large clusters to national hubs, with subsidy and grid-access penalties for non-compliant projects. The Bureau is central to China's effort to convert a fragmented, under-utilized data-center estate into a consolidated national compute grid.

entities.name: Nvidia
entities.desc: Referenced in China AI landscape as the global benchmark domestic Chinese chips must match. Key dynamics: US export controls (Oct 2022, Oct 2023, May 2024, Jan 2025) have progressively restricted H100+ sales to China; 'China-specific' compliant chips (H20, L20) can still be sold at lower specs. Beijing directs major AI firms to defer Nvidia H200 deployment to protect the Huawei Ascend ecosystem. Despite controls, Chinese labs still prefer Nvidia hardware where available — domestic chip gaps in HBM and training efficiency are real. Isaac GR00T (Nvidia's humanoid AI platform) is a strategic anchor for Chinese humanoid OEMs like Unitree and AgiBot despite the chip controls. **Open-weight counter-push (Aug 12):** Released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, an open-weight model, alongside Meta's Muse Glimmer — part of a 20+ company US industry push to contest a category Chinese labs (DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi) currently dominate on adoption and benchmark share. Notably, OpenAI and Anthropic — whose revenue depends on closed, API-sold frontier models — did not sign the coalition letter, underscoring that the open-weight push is as much a hardware-and-distribution play for Nvidia as a model-quality contest.

tags.l: Closure of loophole would boost domestic chip demand
20+ US firms join open-weight coalition vs. China

entities.bio: Founded 1993, Santa Clara (CA), by Jensen Huang (黄仁勋, CEO), Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem. Public (NASDAQ: NVDA). World's dominant AI accelerator chip company; H100/B200/GB300 series are the global benchmark for frontier AI training. Referenced in this landscape due to Chinese AI companies' critical dependence on — and US export controls restricting — Nvidia GPUs.

entities.name: Tsinghua University
entities.desc: **Principal incubator of frontier AI talent and spinouts.** The THUDM lab (Knowledge Engineering Group, Dept of Computer Science), led by Tang Jie (唐杰) and Li Juanzi (李涓子), produced the GLM series of LLMs and directly spun out Zhipu AI (Z.ai, HKEX-listed). Tang Jie and Zhang Peng (CEO of Zhipu) both hold Tsinghua faculty appointments. **Yao Class and IIIS.** The Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Sciences (交叉信息研究院), led by Turing Award winner Yao Qizhi (姚期智/Andrew Yao), runs the Yao Class (姚班) — China's most selective undergraduate CS program and a top-of-funnel talent pipeline for DeepSeek, Zhipu, Baidu, and other frontier labs. **Policy-to-lab pipeline.** Tsinghua hosts national AI labs and joint centers with Huawei, Baidu, and MSRA; faculty routinely serve on AI standards committees consulted by MIIT and MOST; the university's compute infrastructure is a proving ground for domestically-made Huawei Ascend chips.

entities.name: Peking University
entities.desc: **Core NLP and AI research base.** PKU's School of Intelligence Science and Technology and Institute of Computational Linguistics host leading NLP groups with deep ties to Baidu (Robin Li, 李彦宏, is a PKU alum). The Yulan AI lab at PKU produces open-source LLM research widely cited by Chinese frontier labs. **Talent and policy roles.** PKU faculty chair key national AI standards committees and contribute to MOST-funded research programs; the university has a joint AI research center with ByteDance. Wangxuan Institute of Computer Technology (王选计算机研究所) at PKU is a leading center for Chinese-language AI, OCR, and document intelligence — technologies embedded in many Chinese enterprise AI products.

entities.name: USTC
entities.desc: **iFlytek's academic home and quantum AI pioneer.** University of Science and Technology of China, based in Hefei (Anhui). iFlytek founder Liu Qingfeng (刘庆峰) is a USTC alumnus and the university remains iFlytek's primary research partner — USTC-iFlytek joint lab produces the underlying speech and NLP research behind Spark LLM. **National lab ecosystem.** USTC operates under the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) umbrella and hosts the National Laboratory for Physical Sciences at the Microscale and the Anhui Provincial Key Lab for Multimodal Cognitive Computing. It is China's leading institution in quantum information and quantum AI, with direct ties to USTC spin-out Origin Quantum (本源量子). **Strategic compute access.** Hefei's designation as a national AI computing hub gives USTC researchers preferential access to domestic Huawei Ascend-based compute clusters — making it a test bed for post-Nvidia AI training workflows.

entities.name: National Energy Administration (NEA)
entities.desc: China's top energy regulator, under the NDRC — publishes the monthly national electricity-consumption data used as a real-time proxy for industrial activity and, increasingly, AI/data-center compute demand. **July 2026 data (published Aug 14):** Total electricity consumption hit 1.02 trillion kWh, up 8.6% y/y — the first time any country has recorded monthly electricity use above 1 trillion kWh. Secondary industry (manufacturing) consumed 593.6 billion kWh (+4.7% y/y); primary industry rose 20.2% y/y off a small base. NEA and state media attributed the surge to prolonged heatwaves, resilient industrial output, and rising computing-power (算力) and EV-charging load — the same underlying demand driver behind China's AI infrastructure buildout. For investors, the data is a coincident indicator of activity that is harder to game than headline GDP prints, but the heatwave/AC-load component means part of the July spike is weather-driven and won't repeat in cooler months.

tags.l: First country ever to cross 1T kWh/month

entities.name: SMIC
entities.desc: China's largest contract chipmaker (foundry) and the domestic alternative to TSMC for mature and near-leading-edge nodes. **AI spillover pricing power (Aug 14-15):** Management said AI-driven demand is now boosting orders for peripheral chips beyond pure AI accelerators — power management, analog, and other supporting silicon — and that the company sees 'no chance' of cutting prices despite softness in smartphone and auto end-markets. Q2 2026 revenue hit a record $3.0B; wafer shipments rose 14% q/q to 2.9M 8-inch-equivalent units, with average selling price up 5.7% q/q as capacity tightens industry-wide. Shares rose as much as 6.4% in Hong Kong on the print. **Read-through:** The spillover-demand thesis — that AI buildout tightens capacity and pricing well beyond the chips directly used for training and inference — is a structural read on China's semiconductor cycle, though SMIC's mature-node mix means it captures AI-adjacent demand rather than the frontier AI-accelerator market itself, where Huawei's Ascend line (fabbed elsewhere) is the more direct domestic Nvidia alternative. **Bond-yield-driven selloff hits shares (Aug 19, 2026):** SMIC fell 5.16% as the Shanghai Composite dropped 2.40% and Shenzhen Component fell 5.01%, with semiconductor names leading declines (Cambricon -9.64%, Hygon -7.26%, GigaDevice/Hua Hong/NAURA -8% to -12%). The proximate driver was rising government bond yields amid inflation and heavy fiscal-spending/debt-issuance concerns rather than company- or sector-specific news, echoing a simultaneous US/Japan bond selloff. With CXMT and Unitree both having priced blockbuster STAR Market debuts within the prior four weeks, the session is early evidence that China's chip-sector valuations have little cushion against a broader rate-driven risk-off move.

tags.l: "No chance" of price cuts despite phone/auto softness
AI spillover demand hits peripheral/analog chips, not just accelerators

entities.bio: Founded 2000, Shanghai, by Richard Chang (张汝京); current chairman Gao Yonggang, co-CEO Zhao Haijun (赵海军). Public (HKEX: 981, STAR: 688981). China's largest and most advanced pure-play foundry; primary domestic alternative to TSMC, though still generations behind on leading-edge nodes.

entities.name: Apple
entities.desc: Referenced in the China AI landscape as a foreign entrant now training its own model for the China market rather than fully outsourcing to a domestic vendor. **China-specific LLM (Aug 14):** Reported to have trained a proprietary large language model for Apple Intelligence's China rollout with technical assistance from Alibaba, breaking from Apple's earlier approach of relying entirely on a licensed third-party Chinese model. Described as a 'dual-track' strategy — a China-specific model developed with a local partner, alongside its own global models elsewhere — that lets Apple clear Chinese content-review and data-localization requirements while retaining more control over the model than a pure licensing arrangement. Rollout of the resulting AI features in China is expected in the coming months; framed by reporting as a competitive response to Huawei's on-device AI push in the domestic premium-phone market. Terms of the Alibaba arrangement, including data handling and revenue split, have not been disclosed.

tags.l: First foreign firm cleared for a proprietary China AI model
Dual-track strategy: local model + global models elsewhere
Rollout timing and commercial terms undisclosed

entities.bio: Founded 1976, Cupertino, by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne; current CEO Tim Cook. Public (NASDAQ: AAPL). Tracked here for its China AI supply relationship with Alibaba, which trains Apple's China-market LLM for Apple Intelligence.

entities.name: SiEngine
entities.desc: **TianGong 100 (NNA100) mass production, Aug 12, 2026:** Geely-affiliated chipmaker began mass deliveries of its automotive-grade 7nm AI accelerator, designed as a plug-and-play add-on that requires no redesign of a vehicle's electronic/electrical architecture — compatible with cockpit controllers across brands. Delivers 96 TOPS of INT8 compute with 102GB/s of dedicated LPDDR5 bandwidth, enough to run 3B–7B parameter on-device models or several 4B models concurrently; AEC-Q100 Grade 3 and ISO 26262 ASIL-B certified. Priced in the low-thousands-of-yuan range, the company claims the chip cuts total on-vehicle AI deployment cost by roughly half versus dual-control AI-box alternatives — a bet that edge-inference economics, not just raw compute, will decide which domestic chipmakers win the in-cabin AI slot as automakers race to add local large-model assistants.

tags.l: No E/E redesign needed — drop-in for any cockpit controller
Claims ~50% lower deployment cost vs AI-box rivals
Geely-affiliated; independent OEM/Tier-1 order book undisclosed

entities.bio: Founded 2021, Hangzhou, as a joint venture between Geely Holding and Arm China. Private; core products are the Longying (龍鹰一号) automotive SoC series and the TianGong (天工) edge-AI accelerator line, targeting in-vehicle cockpit and assisted-driving compute.

entities.name: Xiaomi
entities.desc: Consumer electronics and smart-EV maker whose Q2 2026 results (reported Aug 19-20) illustrate the memory-chip supercycle's squeeze on device makers rather than just chipmakers. Revenue reached ¥108.9B; net profit fell 20.3% y/y to ¥9.5B and adjusted net profit dropped 42.6% y/y to ¥6.2B as DRAM/memory costs rose faster than Xiaomi anticipated, compressing smartphone gross margin to 8.5% even as smartphone ASP hit a record ¥1,351. **Two-speed business:** Smart EV deliveries rose 28.2% y/y to 104,199 units, cumulative SU7-series deliveries passed 500,000, and the SkyNomad SUV launched — the EV franchise is scaling well ahead of the smartphone unit's margin pressure. **In-house chip hedge:** The Xuanjie O1 SoC, launched 2025, has shipped over 1M units across three device lines, with a next-generation Xuanjie chip due soon — a partial hedge against the same memory-cost inflation (CXMT, Samsung, SK Hynix) squeezing the smartphone segment. Read-through: the AI/memory demand boom that is lifting Chinese memory makers (CXMT) and foundries (SMIC) is simultaneously compressing margins at the device makers who buy that memory — a bifurcation worth tracking across the rest of China's consumer-hardware earnings this quarter.

tags.l: Xuanjie O1 chip ships 1M+ units; next-gen due

entities.bio: Founded 2010, Beijing, by Lei Jun (雷军, CEO). Public (HKEX: 1810). Consumer electronics giant now split between a margin-pressured smartphone business and a fast-growing Smart EV unit (SU7, YU7, SkyNomad); designs its own Xuanjie mobile SoCs in-house.

entities.name: Acorn Robot
entities.desc: Beijing-based embodied-intelligence startup founded late 2024, targeting flexible manufacturing rather than humanoid form factors. **Angel round + Natus AGE-0 launch (Aug 21, 2026):** Raised an angel round led by CM Venture Capital and Nio Capital (with Shuimu Tsinghua Alumni Seed Fund), four months after a ~¥100M ($15M) seed round in March — total funding now several hundred million yuan. Alongside the raise, unveiled Natus AGE-0, a tactile-and-contact-mechanics foundation model for robot manipulation pitched as an alternative to vision-language-action approaches that depend on large demonstration datasets; the company calls the approach 'instinct-driven,' building experience through physical interaction rather than pre-training on collected data. **Business model:** Pursuing Manufacturing-as-a-Service — standardized dual-arm production cells (own sensors, end effectors, and Natus software) sold across multiple customers rather than one-off integration projects; completed a paid proof-of-concept for a global cosmetics ODM. Claims of hardware/task generalization without per-application datasets are self-reported and untested at production scale.

tags.l: Angel round: CM Venture Capital + Nio Capital (Aug 21)
Generalization claims self-reported, unverified at scale

entities.bio: Founded late 2024, Beijing, by Jiang Yao (姜尧) — Tsinghua University mechanical engineering PhD and Harvard neuroscience postdoc — with a team of Tsinghua and Harvard researchers. Private; backed by CM Venture Capital, Nio Capital, and Shuimu Tsinghua Alumni Seed Fund. Core product: Natus AGE-0, a tactile-sensing foundation model for flexible-manufacturing robot arms.

entities.name: X-Humanoid
entities.zh: 北京人形机器人创新中心
entities.desc: State-backed humanoid robotics R&D center designated China's National-Local Jointly Built Embodied Intelligence Robotics Innovation Center (2024); developer of the Tiangong (天工) humanoid platform and the Huisi Kaiwu embodied-AI stack. Raised over ¥700M ($100M) in its first funding round from state-linked vehicles (Beijing Robotics Industry Development Investment Fund, E-Town Capital, Beijing Gaojingjian) plus Baidu as a strategic investor. **World Humanoid Robot Games record-breaking run (Aug 22, 2026 / Issue #97):** Tiangong robots took both the men's-equivalent 100m sprint and standing high jump at the Games' second edition in Beijing — running 9.39 seconds (beating Usain Bolt's 9.58-second human world record) and clearing 2.88m in the standing high jump (versus the 2.45m human record and the prior year's 0.95m robot best). More than 2,000 humanoid robots from competing manufacturers took part across 51 events and 1,000+ competitions over the five-day Games. **Read for positioning:** a competition format engineered around a robot's specific strengths (straight-line sprinting, vertical jump) is a controlled demo, not a proxy for general-purpose task competence — Unitree founder Wang Xingxing said days earlier that humanoids remain less efficient than human workers and must be retrained from scratch for each new task, calling that the industry's central unresolved bottleneck. The Games generate PR and state-showcase value for China's humanoid sector; they don't resolve the generalization question that determines commercial deployment economics.

tags.l: Standing high jump 2.88m vs 2.45m human record

entities.bio: Founded November 2023, Beijing, as Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics Co., Ltd. State-backed (Beijing Robotics Industry Development Investment Fund, E-Town Capital) with Baidu as a strategic investor. Designated China's National-Local Jointly Built Embodied Intelligence Robotics Innovation Center in 2024. Core product: the Tiangong (天工) humanoid platform, now in its 1.2 MAX iteration.
